topics.title: Evaluate a copy-paste output head on July MoE at d512 and d768
topics.body:
Evaluate Copy-Paste Language Models on the original July MoE recipe. The copy head mixes the native vocabulary distribution with a causal distribution over observed tokens, sums repeated-token mass, and uses a learned sink to fall back to the vocabulary head. Packed documents remain isolated. Method: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19247v1.

The first d512, seed-0 validation at 1,000 updates improved the 23-domain macro NLL from 4.579368 to 4.092498 (-0.486869, 10.63%); all 23 domains improved. Native aggregate NLL was 4.387551 versus 3.858693. This is an early, single-seed observation, not a final quality or efficiency claim. The 10,980-update run is still running.

The paired protocol preserves the original July backbone, initialization, QB routing, MuonH/AdamH/Adam optimizer, sequence8192, batch16, tokenizer, training mixture and native validation. Recipe commit: 444b5ea66bda75b6dfc7746ff20c9dfec6ba159a; runtime: 3fd402a926c907d7cb87a04935e56db972652c48. The tiled target-only head adds 525,312 parameters at d512 and avoids materializing a batch × sequence × vocabulary copy distribution. Its attention arithmetic remains quadratic; speedup is not claimed.

Extend the comparison to d768, reusing completed control 2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0. This control has six layers, six query heads, one KV head, expert384/shared768 and deliberately retains the d512 optimizer heuristic. The candidate must keep that recipe, with 1,181,184 added copy-head parameters. Both widths use 10,980 updates (1,439,170,560 input tokens), seed0 and reserved v4-32. Report final and intermediate NLL, all domains, raw loss curves, wall time and throughput; do not equate token matching with compute matching.

Independent dense-mixture checks cover values, all six gradient paths, repeated/absent targets, future/document isolation and disabled-gate parity. All four d512 TPU workers passed BF16 fused-head checks before training. The synthetic precursor reduced loss but failed complete-output evaluation; it did not pass a task mastery gate.

Implementation/evidence: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/pull/152
Frozen protocol: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-moe-protocol.md
First curves and raw-evidence pointers: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-results.md
Live d512 run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/auto-understanding-arch/runs/seed0-v1

The upstream contribution will keep the opt-in copy head and numerical tests separate from the default recipe. Generation/cache support and multiple-seed replication remain outside this initial NLL experiment. A merged implementation does not settle the research question.

Research provenance: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151; originating task definition: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99 (`ordered_paragraph_template@1`). Prior synthetic findings: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/149. These task records provide provenance; the July experiment evaluates native LM data.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Low-effort prior work: the [CPLM paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19247v1) reports gains on other backbones, while this issue reports a 10.63% d512 macro-NLL reduction at 1,000 updates across 23 domains; the full d512 result and paired d768 candidate are still unreported here. Marin's current model uses a fused native-vocabulary loss, and searches for `10229` and `CPLM` found no open Marin implementation PR. The linked research PR, frozen protocol, and W&B run were inaccessible to this session, so their current state and exact measurements remain unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`model.py#L731-L747`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L731-L747) — native loss path
- [`train.py#L173-L193`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/train.py#L173-L193) — tagged per-domain evaluation
- [`launch.py#L207-L246`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/launch.py#L207-L246) — current upstream recipe wiring

# Proposed Fix

1. Recover the linked protocol and pin the exact recipe/runtime commits, dataset and tokenizer identities, validation domains, seeds, optimizer settings, and control/candidate checkpoint IDs for both widths; confirm the d768 control is `2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0` and preserve its d512 optimizer heuristic.
2. Before a d768 run, verify the tiled target-only head against a dense reference for values, six gradient paths, repeated and absent targets, future and packed-document isolation, and disabled-gate parity; repeat the BF16 fused-head check on the target v4-32 setup.
3. Finish or recover the d512 candidate through 10,980 updates, then run the d768 candidate for the same 10,980 updates, seed 0, sequence 8192, and batch 16 on reserved v4-32, changing only the opt-in copy head against each width's control.
4. Publish intermediate and final paired NLL for all 23 domains and both aggregates, raw loss curves, exact token counts, wall time, throughput, parameter and copy-attention cost, and links to immutable configs/checkpoints; distinguish token-matched from compute-matched comparisons.
5. Decide from the final paired results whether the NLL gain justifies measured overhead, then submit a separate opt-in Marin implementation with numerical tests if warranted; leave generation/cache support and replication as explicit follow-ups.

🤖 Draft implementation: #10230. The d768 candidate `428ab40bd4f65ab8758b` is allocated a separate reserved v4-32 slice and its four workers are building; no d768 loss is available yet. It reuses completed d768 control `2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0` without retraining. d512 continues: at 2,000 updates, 23-domain macro NLL is 3.901824 versus 4.278339 (-0.376514); 2,600 training observations are retained with no gaps or non-finite losses. Updated raw curves: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july/update2000/loss-curves.png . These remain intermediate seed-0 comparisons.

🤖 Numerical audit clarification: the pinned research runtime also defaults vocabulary CE to streaming XLA. The research adapter reconstructs log Z using CE plus an FP32 target dot, while XLA obtains the target through matrix multiplication. These are algebraically equivalent but not guaranteed bit-exact. Both runs passed their frozen BF16 value/gradient preflights on all four workers (maximum tested NLL error 0.0009327), which is finite-shape evidence, not an exactness guarantee for all trained states. The upstream PR now exposes only the backend-independent loss and requires caller-supplied NLL/log partition; the frozen training implementations are unchanged. This caveat is recorded in the dated protocol amendment.

🤖 D768 training launch confirmed: run 428ab40bd4f65ab8758b completed four optimizer updates in the retained startup snapshot, with finite losses and all four TPU workers running on a separate v4-32 slice. All four small-shape BF16 preflight checks passed. Full schedule: 10,980 updates; no wall-clock cap. Live run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/auto-understanding-arch/runs/cplm-july-d768-seed0-v1 . Initial curves and evidence: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/tree/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-d768 . Validation starts at update1,000; no d768 quality conclusion yet. Upstream draft #10230 has green CI; five direct numerical tests also pass.

🤖 Final seed-0 results, 2026-10-17 Pacific

Both original-July CPLM runs completed 10,980 optimizer updates / 1,439,170,560 input tokens on TPU v4-32. Historical controls were reused; no baseline was retrained.

| Width | Baseline 23-domain macro NLL | CPLM | Delta | Relative change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| d512 | 3.476994 | 3.336576 | -0.140418 | -4.04% |
| d768 | 3.377656 | 3.255825 | -0.121831 | -3.61% |

Native aggregate eval/loss is 3.304465 → 3.156250 at d512 and 3.209807 → 3.079927 at d768. CPLM has lower macro NLL at all 11 measured validation checkpoints. The margin narrows during training but remains above the frozen 0.01-nat practical threshold at completion. All 23 final domain NLLs are numerically lower; d768 Twitter AAE is effectively flat (-0.000951 nat).

All four workers per candidate succeeded on attempt 0. Both have 10,980 finite loss records without gaps, all scheduled 23-domain validations, matching finished W&B summaries, and committed step-10980 checkpoints. All 297 checkpoint arrays match frozen-config paths/shapes/dtypes and their storage metadata opens; the scalar step reads as 10980. This is a storage/inventory audit, not a full tensor restore.

Updated unsmoothed training and validation curves, per-domain comparisons, raw-data locations/hashes, and completion audits are in the [final report](https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/611073f2/research/cplm-july-results.md).

![d512 raw loss curves](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/611073f2/research/cplm-july/final/loss-curves.png)

![d768 raw loss curves](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/611073f2/research/cplm-july-d768/final/loss-curves.png)

These are single-seed, update/token-matched comparisons, not compute-matched or statistically significant across seeds. D768 retains the historical d512 optimizer heuristic. The frozen mixed-precision adapter's normalizer reconstruction is algebraically equivalent but not bit-exact; the previously recorded small-shape TPU NLL check measured max error 0.000933 and is not a bound for trained full-model states. Prior synthetic full-output failures remain unchanged.

Linked research: [theory #151](https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151), [task #99](https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99), [research PR #152](https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/pull/152), [Marin issue #10229](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10229), [Marin draft PR #10230](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10230). The upstream draft remains scoped to the portable loss and numerical tests; these results do not validate current-trainer integration or generation support.

topics.title: [grug] Hero vibe-check samples pre-switch checkpoints with the current model config
topics.body:
The hero completions sampler stamps every discovered checkpoint with the current `HERO_MODEL_CONFIG`, so after the 16K context switch (#9615) a rebuilt or re-released sample store would sample checkpoints from before step 257553 with `qk_mult` 1.48 instead of the 1.3 they trained with. Nothing flags the mismatch, because `model` is excluded from `sample_id`.

Requests already in the store are safe: `SampleStore.save_request` writes a request only once, and the stored requests for steps 246000, 252000, and 257553 record `qk_mult` 1.3 and `max_seq_len` 4096. The risk appears only when `spec.release` is bumped (the documented backfill knob) or the store root changes.

`sampling_model()` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/vibe_check/config.py` should choose the model per checkpoint. `hero_checkpoint_paths` already reads each ancestor run's W&B config and could carry its `model` along; alternatively the context history could record `qk_mult` per phase.

Found in the independent review of the 16K deploy PR.

topics.title: Time experiment graph setup and isolate Levanter training imports
topics.body:
Report experiment graph construction and execution setup durations, and make training checkpoint types importable without Levanter. Training functions are defined in `marin.training.levanter`; callers import those functions directly from that module. Checkpoint, metrics and pod configuration classes are defined in `marin.training.training`. Existing artifact records identify their result type as `marin.training.training.LevanterCheckpoint`. That class stays at its recorded path so those artifacts load without `ArtifactTypeMismatchError`.

The CatCount RL canary launcher (`python -m experiments.post_training.cat_count_canary`) imports `marin.rl.skyrl` to submit training to Iris. Both import checkpoint types from `marin.training.training`. Importing either the launcher or `marin.rl.skyrl` loads no Levanter, Transformers, Torch or W&B module. On October 15, `python -X importtime -c 'import marin.rl.skyrl'` reported 22.19 seconds on main and 4.24 seconds on this branch (one fresh interpreter each; cache warmth was not controlled). These are local import measurements; coordinator startup in Iris has not been measured.

Commands using `marin.experiment.cli` configure INFO logging when the root logger has no handlers. Their INFO log messages report elapsed graph-construction time as `experiment/build`, including when printing a plan without `--run`. With `--run`, `marin.execution.lazy.run` also times provenance collection and graph lowering once per call (`execution/provenance`, `execution/lower`), and dependency expansion for each requested step (`execution/expand`). [RL startup design](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/596). Outside Iris, `--run` on an RL command built with `marin.rl.cli`, such as the CatCount launcher, submits an Iris coordinator job that reruns the command; the `execution/*` messages appear in that job's log.

`lib/iris` requires `marin-iris-native` 0.1.13.dev38952644761 or later. Its public proxy applies an identity's `auth.user_roles` entry before `auth.admin_users` and the default role, matching the Python role policy.

For dense Qwen, a test imports `marin.rl.cli` in a fresh interpreter and fails if Levanter, Transformers, Torch or W&B is loaded; a separate fresh-interpreter import of `experiments.post_training.cat_count_canary.launcher` on October 16 at `0393bc96` loaded none of them. Snowball and Hero launchers import training functions, such as `resolve_training_env` and `run_levanter_train_lm`, from `marin.training.levanter`, and checkpoint and configuration records from `marin.training.training`. Every class and function in those two modules has the same AST as in main's `marin.training.training`, so Snowball and Hero need no model-specific numerical check for these import and timing changes.

topics.title: [evaldash] SOTOPIA samples hide traces and mislabel continuous rewards
topics.body:
EvalDash cannot display SOTOPIA conversations from Harbor runs, although the trial artifacts contain the complete transcript. It also presents SOTOPIA's continuous reward through binary `Correct` and `Incorrect` filters without explaining the threshold.

Affected run: [Snowball SOTOPIA-hard](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261003-131920-open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02-sotopia-hard-2863/samples?task=hf%3A%2F%2Fopen-athena%2Fsotopia-hard-harbor&filter=incorrect&i=27).

Reproduce:
1. Open the affected run and select any sample.
2. Observe `No trajectory recorded for this sample.`
3. Inspect the sealed FineStore `samples` table under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261003-131920-open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02-sotopia-hard-2863/results`.
4. Observe 100 `agentic` rows and 100 null `trajectory_uri` values.
5. Inspect a matching Harbor trial, for example `harbor_jobs/harbor_hf___open-athena_sotopia-hard-ha_c928c249d99a/sotopia-01h7vkqht745xap1a4ddv8h4__xwVQFXm/attempts/000/agent/sotopia-summary.json`. It contains the full `transcript`, evaluator `reasoning`, per-dimension `scores`, and context-budget data.
6. Compare the run metadata and sample classification. The run declares primary metric `reward` with `metric_kind=continuous` and reports mean reward `0.309`. FineStore contains 99 `correct=false` rows and one `correct=true` row because Harbor defines solved as reward ≥0.99.

Expected: EvalDash shows the retained SOTOPIA transcript, evaluator reasoning, and dimension scores for each sample. A continuous-reward task should emphasize the numeric reward. Binary filters should be hidden or named `Solved` and `Not solved`, with the 0.99 threshold stated.

The format mismatch remains on current Harbor main. The SOTOPIA agent writes [`sotopia-summary.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/1d29d200414b6488a87192f50f617b1b5bd4b6f4/src/harbor/agents/installed/sotopia.py#L24-L25) and directs its runner to that file ([lines 126–134](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/1d29d200414b6488a87192f50f617b1b5bd4b6f4/src/harbor/agents/installed/sotopia.py#L126-L134)). The archive only records a trajectory when `agent/trajectory.json` exists ([lines 256–281](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/1d29d200414b6488a87192f50f617b1b5bd4b6f4/src/harbor/archive.py#L256-L281)). It maps reward ≥0.99 to the sample's `correct` field ([lines 49–109](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/1d29d200414b6488a87192f50f617b1b5bd4b6f4/src/harbor/archive.py#L49-L109)). EvalDash then exposes that field as generic `correct` and `incorrect` filters ([sample outcome code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1290cfb5e128214b7225bc7b0e98ac1e0a8044dc/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/web/src/utils/samples.ts#L5-L36)).

topics.title: [Evals] Select and implement the Marin AA-II validation suite
topics.body:
## Goal

Select and implement a pinned, open, text-only validation suite that approximates the capabilities in the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index across Marin pretraining, mid-training, and post-training checkpoints.

This is the concrete successor to #6050 and the eval-selection workstream under #6503. It is a **generative validation suite for both base/pretraining and post-trained checkpoints**, complementary to the lightweight PPL competency proxies in #5819. Benchmark items must remain isolated from training data, while results should be available alongside regular pretraining validation dashboards.

The suite is a proxy, not a reproduction of Artificial Analysis: several AA datasets and grading harnesses are private, and agentic behavior cannot be faithfully reduced to text-only tasks.

## Proposed benchmark mapping

| AA benchmark | Open text-only replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GDPval-AA v2** | **FinanceBench + IFBench + DS-1000** | Composite proxy for professional analysis, constraint-following, and practical technical work. There is no good single text-only equivalent for GDPval's agentic knowledge work and file outputs. |
| **τ³-Banking** | **τ²-Bench-Verified Retail** | Closest match for stateful customer-service workflows, policy adherence, and tool use. Use **BFCL** only as an easier, weaker fallback. |
| **Terminal-Bench v2.1** | **OT-TBench-Lite** | Direct lightweight terminal-agent proxy. |
| **SciCode** | **DS-1000 + CruxEval** | DS-1000 covers practical scientific/data coding; CruxEval adds code-execution reasoning. |
| **Humanity's Last Exam** | **MMLU-Pro + OlympiadBench Math** | MMLU-Pro supplies broad coverage; OlympiadBench supplies the hard tail. |
| **GPQA Diamond** | **MMLU-Pro science subset** | Easy to run but weaker than GPQA. Retaining open **GPQA Diamond** itself is the more faithful option if contamination policy permits. |
| **CritPt** | **OlympiadBench Physics** | Best simple open physics proxy, though exam-level rather than research-level. |
| **AA-Omniscience** | **Open factual QA with abstention and negative marking** | Use a SimpleQA-style or TriviaQA-derived held-out set; score correct `+1`, abstain `0`, incorrect `−1`. Report accuracy and hallucination rate separately as well as the signed score. |
| **AA-LCR** | **MRCR** | Good open long-context proxy, though more retrieval-oriented than AA-LCR's document synthesis. Cover the intended 10K–100K-token range. |

Artificial Analysis methodology: https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking

## Scoring proposal

- Preserve the current AA component weights so the proxy has a stable composite: GDPval proxy 20%, τ³ proxy 14%, Terminal proxy 16%, SciCode proxy 8%, HLE proxy 12%, GPQA proxy 6%, CritPt proxy 6%, Omniscience proxy 12%, and LCR proxy 6%.
- For composite replacements, normalize each constituent metric and macro-average within the component before applying the component weight.
- Publish every component score alongside the aggregate. Call the aggregate **Marin AA-II proxy**, never an AA score.
- Treat the weights and task revisions as a versioned configuration so the suite remains reproducible when AA or upstream benchmarks change.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Confirm dataset availability, licenses, canonical splits, and exact benchmark variants; pin dataset and harness revisions.
- [ ] Add explicit eval-only manifests and contamination metadata. No benchmark test item may enter training or core PPL tracking, consistent with #5819.
- [ ] Implement each component behind Marin's standard OpenAI-compatible eval entrypoint and make the suite selectable by one versioned config in #6503.
- [ ] Pin prompts/chat templates, decoding parameters, parsers/graders, seeds, repeats, tokenizer/model revisions, and context lengths.
- [ ] Emit raw per-item outputs plus component metrics, confidence intervals, runtime/cost, failure counts, and the versioned composite score.
- [ ] Provide a tiny deterministic smoke subset for scheduled regression testing, plus the full-suite path.
- [ ] Run a representative model panel and measure repeatability and rank correlation against available AA/Harbor component results. Document where the text-only proxy fails to preserve rankings.
- [ ] Publish results through the eval results/leaderboard path tracked by #6043 and #6503.
- [ ] Document how to add, replace, or retire a component without silently changing historical scores.

## Related work

- #6050 — original AA-II eval TBD (closed in favor of July work)
- #6503 — automated eval system parent Epic
- #6863 — July Evalchemy/Harbor execution work
- #5819 — lightweight PPL proxies for AA-measured competencies; complementary to this generative checkpoint suite
- #7090 — broader new-evals wish-list, including scalable proxies for several AA components

- CC BY-NC datasets are acceptable, although none remain in the current shortlist.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDPval professional work | IFBench | [allenai/IFBench_test](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/IFBench_test) | ODC-BY 1.0 | Deterministic prompt-level constraint accuracy |

| τ³-Banking | τ²-Bench-Verified Retail | [amazon-agi/tau2-bench-verified](https://github.com/amazon-agi/tau2-bench-verified) | MIT | Deterministic task success from state/action checks |

| SciCode | CruxEval | [facebookresearch/cruxeval](https://github.com/facebookresearch/cruxeval) | MIT | Execution pass@1 for input/output prediction |
| HLE breadth | MMLU-Pro non-science categories | [TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) | MIT | Gold multiple-choice accuracy |
| HLE hard math tail | OlympiadBench Math, English text-only open-ended subset | [OpenBMB/OlympiadBench](https://github.com/OpenBMB/OlympiadBench) | MIT in GitHub; Apache 2.0 in Hugging Face metadata | Exact, numeric, or symbolic answer accuracy |
| GPQA scientific reasoning | MMLU-Pro biology, chemistry, and physics categories | [TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) | MIT | Gold multiple-choice accuracy |

| Omniscience | SimpleQA | [OpenAI simple-evals](https://github.com/openai/simple-evals) | MIT | Deterministic normalized gold match with correct `+1`, abstain `0`, incorrect `-1`; reference-answer conditional loss/PPL for base checkpoints |
| Long-context reasoning | MRCR | [openai/mrcr](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr) | MIT | Deterministic gold-answer similarity by context length and needle count |

FinanceBench, TriviaQA, BFCL, GPQA Diamond, and direct AA datasets are out of scope. MMLU-Pro is partitioned so the HLE and GPQA proxies do not score the same questions twice. Reference-answer conditional loss/PPL is an auxiliary base-checkpoint metric; generated-answer accuracy remains the post-training metric.

The first definition-of-done item remains open until the exact dataset and harness revisions, splits, and OlympiadBench configurations are pinned.

For the missing benchmarks identified in the AA-II coverage cross-check, we opened five adapter/benchmark PRs:

**Evalchemy (text-only benchmarks):**
- **OlympiadBench** (HLE hard tail + CritPt proxy): https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/24
- **MRCR** (AA-LCR long-context retrieval proxy): https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/22
- **FinanceBench** (GDPval proxy component): https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/25
- **IFBench** (GDPval proxy component): https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/23

**Harbor (agentic benchmark):**
- **τ²-Bench-Verified Retail** (τ³-Banking proxy): https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/10

Coverage report with per-component gap analysis: [notes/marin/aa2_eval_coverage.md](https://github.com/openshoulders/OpenThoughts-Agent/blob/main/notes/marin/aa2_eval_coverage.md)

Still missing from the proposed suite: **OlympiadBench Physics** is partially covered by the OlympiadBench evalchemy PR (math + physics subfields), but the dedicated OlympiadBench Physics split for CritPt may need a separate filter.

@Helw150 — these are draft PRs ready for review. Happy to iterate on dataset pinning, grading harnesses, or scoring configs.

^ Reviewed the Evalchemy above. For MRCR and IFBench, the LLM Agent that implemented them seems to have hallucinated benchmarks rather than ingested the above. For OlympiadBench, it implemented custom scoring that has a few mistakes v.s. the benchmarks repo. FinanceBench it didn't include the PDFs which the questions are in reference to so the questions are mostly unanswerable without their corresponding docs IIUC.

topics.title: [inference] Add matched native and vLLM checkpoint fixtures
topics.body:
Export small Snowball and Hero BF16 checkpoints and benchmark the same weights and token workload in Levanter and the promoted Marin vLLM fork. Verify every exported tensor through native loading. Retain checkpoint identity, configuration, runtime topology, effective execution modes, and generated-token hashes. A separate non-unit normalization fixture changes only norm weights and records its seed and affected tensors.

Use packed expert banks, isolate Triton caches, and bound Ninja/nvcc concurrency. Expose expert parallelism, bounded KV memory, and eager or compiled execution. An optional hashed FlashInfer cache wheel loads and hashes precompiled MoE libraries with JIT disabled, preserving backend selection and autotuning. Setup and warmup remain outside measured samples.

The compare command verifies checkpoint, architecture, dtype, exact workload, and accelerator allocation, including native EP versus vLLM DP/EP or TPU SPMD data parallelism. Validate Grug aliases and derived defaults while retaining raw configuration differences. An untimed validation batch identifies the first divergent token; mismatched outputs suppress throughput ratios.

Bounded Snowball diagnostics compare shared-prefix logits, router precision, actual layer activations, and independent FP64 head reprojections. Native tracing records its effect on logits; named worker RPC captures every vLLM DP rank. Ordinary-engine generation independently varies embedding-gate SiLU and sigmoid precision without activation tracing. On H100, sigmoid-only FP32 matches all 32 vLLM tokens for both all-one and non-unit norm fixtures; promoting both functions still fails the non-unit fixture. Shared training and serving defaults are unchanged. An exhaustive standalone diagnostic evaluates all 65,280 finite BF16 sigmoid inputs against an independent FP64 reference, separating normal, subnormal, and saturated outputs. Both CPU runtimes execute successfully; fourteen focused tests and the delta affected-test run pass. Accelerator unary validation remains pending.

H100 EP2 tiny eager Hero produces identical 32 tokens using marin-community/vllm#83. On v5p, the combined short-convolution/cache stack passes twelve cases, then both runtimes produce identical 32 tokens for the same tiny Hero checkpoint with data parallelism four and tensor/expert parallelism one. Native measures 790.72 output tokens/second and eager vLLM 358.54 (2.205× for this workload only). The two-layer fixture exercises local and global attention because the final layer is always global. The measured pins, workload, and production Hero memory accounting are in the inference design docs.

GB200 Snowball starts with precompiled FlashInfer kernels and JIT disabled: 54.64 seconds of model/cache setup and a 12.01 GiB sampled cgroup peak under the unchanged 48 GiB limit. Unmodified Snowball outputs still disagree across runtimes, so its ratios remain withheld. Production checkpoints and Hero CUDA graphs remain unvalidated. Stacked on #9661. Part of #7219.

topics.title: [taskcompendium] Merge output_paths, collect, and artifacts into one capture
topics.body:
The rollout engine must keep the task machine, and the agent that used it, alive until grading ends. The engine copies `TaskSpec.output_paths` from the task machine, then passes the live machine to `grade_in_sandbox`. For a `ScriptGrader`, `grade_in_sandbox` runs the `collect` commands on that machine and copies the `artifacts` out before it starts the verifier machine (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py:512`, `:528`, `:545`). Thus the engine cannot close the task machine while the verifier runs, and an agent that is still running can change files before the grader copies them.

Three fields say what to take from the task machine. Each has a different owner, limit, and destination:

- `TaskSpec.output_paths`: files returned in `Rollout.outputs` and given to every grader at the same paths. The limit is 1,024 files and 16 MiB in total, because the rollout holds them in memory.
- `ScriptGrader.collect`: commands that run as root on the task machine to make grader inputs. Only the SWE importer uses them, to write the agent's change as a patch (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/swe.py:51`).
- `ScriptGrader.artifacts`: files or directories copied into the verifier machine only. The limit is 1 GiB and 100,000 files. Users: the SWE patch, the whole workspace of the tasktrove repository-build tasks (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/tasktrove/repository_build.py:105`), and `/testbed` in the Harbor tests (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_harbor.py:632`).

Proposed: replace the three fields with one task-level capture that the engine runs once, after the harness ends.

```python
class CapturePath(BaseModel):
    path: str                       # a file or a directory on the task machine
    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()   # patterns to skip inside a directory
    required: bool = False          # True: a missing path fails the capture


class Capture(BaseModel):
    commands: tuple[VerifierCommand, ...] = ()  # run first, as root, on the task machine
    paths: tuple[CapturePath, ...] = ()
```

The capture writes each path into one local directory, at its original location. The rollout points to that directory, and every grader reads only from it. An in-process grader reads the files, and a script grader's verifier machine gets them at the same paths. The engine can then close the task machine and stop the agent while grading runs, and wait for both at the end. A failed close or stop stays a cleanup error and does not change the grade. Captures are on disk at every size, so small files and large directories need no separate fields. State that is not a file must be written to a file by a capture command, for example with `pg_dump` or `curl localhost:8080 > response.txt`.

To decide:

- Who deletes the capture directory. A proposal: `run_task` deletes it after grading, unless the caller asks to keep it to grade again later. The caller of a rollout without grading owns it.
- The size limit. Today's artifact limit (1 GiB, 100,000 files) is a starting point.
- The TaskCompendium grading API in two steps, `capture(task, machine)` and `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, which the curation pipelines (`grade_task`) also use.

Related: #9763 and #9978 ask to grade a supplied final state without model inference. With the two-step API, that is `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, where the captured directory comes from a builder or from the capture of a prepared machine. This came up in the harness redesign of #10203.

Done when:

- `TaskSpec` has one capture field, and `output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts` are removed, with a new schema version.
- No grader receives the task machine: `grade_in_sandbox` reads the captured directory.
- The engine closes the task machine and stops the agent while it grades, and a failed close or stop is a cleanup error.
- The SWE importer, the tasktrove repository-build tasks, and every `output_paths` user are migrated, and their tests pass.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The engine captures `output_paths` after the turn loop, but `grade_in_sandbox` runs `ScriptGrader.collect` and copies `artifacts` later, while it still holds the task machine. The attempt's resource stack closes the episode and task machine after grading, so the verifier is coupled to a live, mutable workspace. The existing output capture is limited to 1,024 files/16 MiB in memory; artifact transfer uses a separate tar path with a 1 GiB/100,000-member limit.

**Relevant code**
- [`models.py#L580-L614`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L580-L614) — grader-owned collection fields
- [`output_capture.py#L14-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/output_capture.py#L14-L54) — in-memory output limit
- [`grading.py#L499-L558`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L499-L558) — live-machine collection during grading
- [`engine.py#L392-L414`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L392-L414) — capture and grade order
- [`harbor_export.py#L210-L235`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/experiments/post_training/task_curation/tasktrove/harbor_export.py#L210-L235) — repository artifact assumption

# Design: one task capture

## Goal

Each attempt should make one bounded, local snapshot of the task machine after the agent finishes. Grading, including repeat grading of a supplied final state, should use that snapshot without receiving the task machine. This is a design-level change across TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, curation, and task authors; it needs a dedicated implementation PR after the harness contract in [#10203](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203) settles. No open PR targets #10225; [#9838](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9838) covers the related supplied-state path and should be reconciled with the new capture API.

## Design and implementation order

1. Add `TaskSpec.capture: Capture` with ordered `commands` and `CapturePath(path, exclude, required)`, then remove `TaskSpec.output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts`. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` from 0.27 and reject old serialized tasks. Validate normalized absolute paths, reject overlaps with private verifier roots and overlapping capture roots, and keep the original absolute path as the grader destination. Commands run in order as root after the episode is quiescent.
2. Make `capture(task, machine)` produce an owned local directory, with files and empty directories laid out relative to `/`. Reuse the artifact tar extraction's link/path checks and preserve modes and timestamps. Enforce one aggregate 1 GiB/100,000-member budget across all paths; an optional missing path is omitted, a required missing path or unsafe member is a submission failure, and command or machine failure remains an infrastructure error. Capture once, then read only the local directory. A direct `grade(task, attempt, captured)` entry point and the curation `grade_task` wrapper should share the same grader dispatch; neither receives `Machine`.
3. Port the engine onto #10203's `run_task`/harness surface. End the episode's ability to write to the task machine and wait for its agent to stop **before** capture, including on turn-limit and timeout paths; copying while an agent can still write would leave the race in place. After capture, start task-machine cleanup while grading reads the local directory, then await cleanup before returning. Keep close/stop failures in `cleanup_errors` without changing a completed grade. Change harness grading so a `SessionGrader` reads the immutable rollout and capture, not a live episode or machine.
4. Define ownership so `run_task` removes the directory after grading by default and returns no dangling path; an explicit retain option transfers cleanup to the caller. A rollout that runs without grading transfers ownership to its caller. The returned rollout can name a capture directory only when it is retained. Keep `GradingAttempt.state` for caller-supplied JSON state; machine state needed by a grader must be written to a captured file by a command.
5. Migrate the SWE patch command, tasktrove repository-build workspace, ARC and tasktrove `output_paths` constructors, Harbor export, curation controls and audit projections, `direct_chat`, serialized fixtures, and rollout documentation. Regenerate persisted TaskSpec rows at the new schema version. Coordinate with [#9784](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9784), whose open Taskforge spec builder still names `output_paths`, and adapt #9838's prepared-state flow to call the same capture and grade functions.

## Validation

Test missing and excluded paths, aggregate budgets, links and path traversal, file modes, and an empty directory. An end-to-end attempt should prove that changing or closing the task machine after capture cannot change the grade, and that close failures preserve the grade while appearing in cleanup diagnostics. Exercise SWE patch grading, tasktrove repository grading, curation's supplied-state path, and the Harbor export contract. Run the TaskCompendium and RolloutEngine suites, affected curation tests, type checking, and the repository pre-commit gates before a PR.

## Open question

The proposed 1 GiB/100,000-member budget is global, unlike today's per-artifact check. Measure a representative tasktrove repository capture before fixing that limit; if it exceeds the budget, put an explicit larger cap in the task capture contract rather than silently truncating it.

topics.title: [experiments] Move the HPC Fund venv to jax 0.11.1 with jax-triton
topics.body:
The AMD HPC Fund venv recipe now installs jax and jaxlib 0.11.1 with ROCm 10.1 and `jax_rocm10_plugin` 0.11.1+rocm10.1.0, plus Levanter's jax-triton 0.3.1 and triton 3.6.0 pins. jaxlib 0.11.0 does not load `jax_rocm10_plugin`'s kernel modules, so `jax_triton` kernels cannot run in a venv built from the current recipe. One example is the Grug routing top-k that #9942 uses for QBRoutedMoE.

`run_gpu.sh` now sets `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1`. Jobs inherit `/opt/rocm-7.2.0` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` from the cluster's default module, so they load its HIP runtime and RCCL instead of the wheel's. With jax 0.11.1 on those libraries, RCCL aborts at the first collective with `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 must be set`. Removing `/opt/rocm` from the paths also avoids the abort, but on one MI350X it makes `jax.lax.top_k` on rows under 1,024 entries 2.4-4.2x slower: 2.4 ms against 1.0 ms at [65536, 384] with k=9, and 1.7 ms against 0.40 ms at [32768, 256] with k=5. The wrapper therefore keeps the cluster libraries.

On one 8x MI350X node, with venvs built command for command from main's recipe and from this one, a cross-device psum in the new venv with the cluster libraries kept aborts as above when `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM` is unset and passes when it is set. The June synthetic benchmark (`--size full --expert-axis 8 --batch-size 64 --steps 20`, `RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton`), one run each, median of steps 2-19:

| Recipe and wrapper | Step time | MFU | Step 0 | Loss at step 19 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main: jax 0.11.0, ROCm 10.0 | 2.614 s | 8.64% | 341 s | 11.7769 |
| this PR: jax 0.11.1, ROCm 10.1 | 2.626 s | 8.60% | 312 s | 11.7770 |

Part of #9812.

comments.body: 🤖 With jax-triton installed, any jax_triton kernel that a multi-GPU AMD run launches will hang it. On ROCm, a jax_triton kernel fails the first time one process launches it on several GPUs at once: jaxlib 0.11.1 reads the compiled hsaco from a temporary file and deletes it without holding its cache lock, so all but one GPU fail and the step stalls at the next collective. Details and a standalone repro: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9853#issuecomment-6090140907. The June benchmark above passed because nothing in it launches a jax_triton kernel: the ring MoE path calls none, and routing still uses `lax.top_k`. These would: #9942's routing top-k in `QBRoutedMoE`, the Sonic kernels that `ep_ragged_all_to_all` and `ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all` use whenever `sonic_gather_sum_available()` is true (it is on AMD once jax-triton is installed), and `short_conv`'s Triton backend for models that use it. On its own this recipe is fine for the ring path; with #9942, or with the ragged or pooled MoE paths, it is not until AMD's jax fork fixes the race.

topics.title: Hero Run: Sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval
topics.body: Issue to track the investigation into the sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval PTB is in general OOD data due to token, 'N' token, and all lowercase. Among other quirks. Initial hypothesises: 1. Some in-context learning capacity turned on for a checkpoint. 2. Data contam/very similar article in training data around then. 3. Some very rare tokens in PTB happened to get upweighted on a checkpoint that under normal checkpoints are heavily penalized. 4. Other/Unk Artifact comparing first 4k tokens: https://claude.ai/artifact/W82uDiQuQygwAaqfX3hEiR Most noteworthy drop is: "los angeles financier marvin" " mar" for marvin is predicted with 80% confidence on the overperforming checkpoint- seems likely that the exact phrase los angeles financier marvin appeared in the training data. It then dropped back down to its usual 0.2% on the following checkpoint. Completions API with prompt for every checkpoint: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/hero-completions/latest/index.html#a=1ed4a3edd3645961c051e72c8b85a9ec7b6fbea0f2c5b3a27960cc1c806b237d&b=dde26b9fe079446f0c76ecc1b7f469d59815aca5f3f3c84f50a3993df7a26978&prompt=biocorpus-protein-design-heldout

comments.body: 'mar' was at 15% on checkpoint 198k. And the model always knows mar ->vin ->d ->avis. So the person marvin davis is cleanly in the training data for a while. Google search-> "Marvin Davis was a prominent Beverly Hills billionaire, oil tycoon, and corporate buyout artist who made massive waves as Wall Street's highest-paid financier in 1989." Any docs related to news ongoings in Los Angeles may be spiking the eval.

PTB is '1989 Wall Street Journal (WSJ) articles'. We want our model to understand what happened in the 1980s in general.. so having the facts of this eval in the training data is intentional. Will see what comes up from scanning our data in this 6k step range.

🤖 **Data scan result: PTB's own text was in the training stream ~500 steps before the 210k checkpoint (hypothesis 2, contamination).**

**Method.** I rebuilt the hero's exact training stream from the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 mix stages, and the block shuffle. Then I read every sequence trained in steps **204,000–216,000**: 12,000 steps × 11,264 sequences × 4,096 tokens, about 554B tokens over 48 CPU jobs on cw-us-east-02a. The scan searched for PTB-specific lowercase phrases, their normal-cased counterparts, and runs of ` <unk>`.

**Result.** A block of about **231 sequences (~1M tokens)** in source **`c13q3`** at **steps 209,272–209,669** contains Penn Treebank text expanded into sliding n-gram windows (`<s> <s> … <word>` per line). It reads like an NLP exercise repository: it also has NMT training notes and scraped request headers. It includes the exact sentences in our PTB eval, e.g. `los angeles financier marvin`, `in london british airways chairman lord king`, `the stock of ual corp. continued`, `the dow industrials were off N points`. A related source, `c28q1`, has n-gram log-probability tables over the same text around step 206.3k (`lg P(corp. | acquire ual)`).

| Lowercase PTB-format hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `los angeles financier` | 3 | 0 |
| `british airways chairman` | 3 | 0 |
| `ual corp` | 26 | 0 |

Normal-cased news about the same entities appears about equally in both ranges:

| Normal-cased hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `Marvin Davis` | 331 | 332 |
| `UAL Corp` | 226 | 230 |
| `British Airways chairman` | 25 | 27 |

So general knowledge of the 1989 story is steady. What changed before 210k is exposure to the PTB text itself, which the checkpoint partly retained and which had faded by 216k. "Lord King" alone produced thousands of false positives ("Sovereign Lord King James…"), so those hits are excluded.

**300-character chunks: PTB eval text vs. the training document**

PTB (Paloma `ptb` val):
```
this is a total <unk> for takeover-stock traders one investment banker said 
 los angeles financier marvin davis who put united in play with a $ N billion bid two months ago last night <unk> both a ray of hope and an extra element of uncertainty by saying he remains interested in acquiring ual 
 but
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,550):
```
 traders one investment
for takeover-stock traders one investment banker
takeover-stock traders one investment banker said
<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> los
<s> <s> <s> <s> los angeles
<s> <s> <s> los angeles financier
<s> <s> los angeles financier marvin
<s> los angeles financier <NAME>
los angeles financier
```

PTB:
```
in london british airways chairman lord king was quoted in the times as declaring he is not prepared to take my shareholders into a <unk> deal 
 observers said it appeared that british air was angered at the way the bid has <unk> into confusion as well as by the banks ' effort to round up financing 
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,665):
```
<s> <s> <s> <s> in london
<s> <s> <s> in london british
<s> <s> in london british airways
<s> in london british airways chairman
in london british airways chairman lord
london british airways chairman lord king
british airways chairman lord king was
airways chairman lord king was quoted
chairman lor
```

The training copy has "marvin davis" replaced with `<NAME>` in most windows, presumably by PII scrubbing. One window, `los angeles financier marvin`, kept the first name because the scrubber only caught "marvin davis" as a pair. That is the token the 210k checkpoint predicted at 0.80. It also explains why every checkpoint already completes `marvin → davis`: that part is general knowledge, not this document.

**Takeaways**
- The 210k drop in PTB loss (about −0.2 nats, spread across almost every line) comes from verbatim exposure to the eval text in an n-gram layout roughly 330–730 steps earlier. It is not a capability change. 210k still misses PTB's genuinely surprising words ("declaring", "my"), which fits brief, partial exposure.
- Paloma PTB is contaminated in the hero mix, at least in `c13q3` and `c28q1`. Its curve will spike whenever those windows come up in the data order, so it shouldn't be read as a quality signal. Wikitext-103 and the other public eval sets may warrant the same scan.

Raw hits: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/full/*.jsonl`. Scanner: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/scan_training_data.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`, not pushed.

🤖 **The contaminated document, and every step that reads it**

**What it is.** One GitHub repository dump in source `c13q3`, **`quanpn90/torch-nplm`**: a Torch implementation of Bengio et al. (2003), with the name scrubbed to `<NAME>` in the README. It is **1,385,899 tokens** (4.83M characters), a single BOS…EOS document that spans 340 training sequences of 4,096 tokens.

| File | Characters |
|---|---|
| README.md | 260 |
| extract_ngrams.py | 2,308 |
| train.lua | 12,261 |
| **data/ptb/test.6grams** | **2,543,118** |
| **data/ptb/valid.6grams** | **2,262,165** |
| util/BatchLoader.lua | 4,901 |
| util/IdentityLinear.lua | 985 |

About 99.6% of the document is the **full PTB test and validation sets as sliding 6-gram windows**. `valid.6grams` starts `<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> consumers / … / consumers may want to move their / may want to move their telephones …`, which is exactly the start of Paloma's `ptb` eval document. So the whole Paloma PTB eval set is in the training data, with each word appearing in 6 overlapping windows.

First 500 characters:
```
Repository: quanpn90/torch-nplm

File: README.md
# torch-nplm

Neural probabilistic language model (<NAME>, 2003) implemented in Torch.

GPU supported for fast training.

Hierarchical supported for fast softmax-ing on a large vocabulary. 

HSM borrowed from https://github.com/yoonkim/lstm-char-cnn


File: extract_ngrams.py
#!/usr/bin/python
import sys

# This script extracts n-grams from a set of PREPROCESSED text files (train, set, valid)

data_dir = sys.argv[1]
ngram_order = int(sys.argv[2])

tra
```

**Every step that reads it over the full 390,251-step schedule.** I inverted the mixture and block shuffle using the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 stages, and `c13q3` at 69.8M sequences per epoch. The document straddles two 256-sequence shuffle blocks, which land in different shuffle windows, so each epoch reads it in two bursts:

| Epoch | Document part | Sequences | Steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | **176,080–176,355** |
| 0 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams` (Paloma PTB)** | 228 | **209,390–209,669** |
| 1 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | 327,205–327,493 *(future)* |
| 1 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams`** | 228 | **362,280–362,578** *(future)* |

**Implications**
- The 210k checkpoint was saved about 330–610 steps after the hero trained on the entire Paloma PTB eval set. That explains the drop, and its fading by 216k.
- **The PTB eval should drop again right after step ~362.3k**, when epoch 1 reaches the same block; that's in the cooldown stage. It's a useful sanity check that this explanation is right. The ~176k and ~327k bursts carry only PTB test-split text, not the Paloma eval text.
- Other copies of PTB in the mix, for example the n-gram probability tables in `c28q1` around step 206.3k, aren't covered by this mapping. A dedup or decontamination pass against Paloma would find them.

Files: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/docs/` holds the full document text (`doc_209550_4116.txt`), `summary.json`, and `torch_nplm_steps.json`, which maps every read to its step and row. Scripts: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/{scan_training_data,find_training_doc,find_doc_steps}.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`.
Its https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/, specifically https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/blob/master/data/ptb/valid.6grams. The sort of doc that could induce very weird repetition behavior.

@ClassicLarry, I went through the public W&B evals: all 16 Paloma and 7 Uncheatable subsets, every eval from step 2,999 to 227,999. I also ran the decon matcher on the torch-nplm files. Here are four results that may help the scan. **1. PTB has drops the torch-nplm reads don't explain** | Evals | PTB loss | Note | |---|---|---| | 101,999 → **104,999** → 107,999 | 2.143 → **1.961** → 2.109 | A one-eval drop with no mapped read nearby | | 188,999 → **191,999** | 2.115 → **2.015** | Drops 0.10 and stays below 2.08 through 227,999 | | 173,999 → **176,999** → 179,999 | 2.141 → **2.099** → 2.114 | Just after the 176,080–176,355 read, which has only the PTB *test* split | | 203,999 → **206,999** → 209,999 | 2.079 → **1.903** → 1.712 | The first half comes before the 209,390 read; it fits the `c28q1` tables at ~206.3k | The 176,999 row is a natural control. That read had PTB test text but none of the eval sentences. It moved the eval 0.029 below the average of its two neighbours, while the curve otherwise stays between 2.113 and 2.141 from 155,999 to 188,999. By the same measure, 104,999 is 0.165 below its neighbours, close to 209,999's 0.187. So I'd guess another copy of the validation text was read in steps **102,000–104,999**. If your scanner can run on that range, and on **189,000–191,999**, that would test it. **2. WikiText-103 shows the same pattern; general Wikipedia doesn't** At steps 125,999 / 128,999 / 131,999 / 134,999, `wikitext_103` reads 1.707 / **1.558** / 1.638 / 1.684. Over the same evals, `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` reads 1.828 / 1.827 / 1.823 / 1.824. Smaller one-sided drops recur at 137,999, 152,999, 203,999 and 212,999–215,999. None of them shows up in m2d2_wikipedia. A 0.15 drop on the WikiText eval with flat general Wikipedia looks like a document containing the eval text itself, not a Wikipedia-heavy stretch. Candidate windows: - **126,000–128,999**; - **210,000–212,999**, which your 204k–216k scan already covers. Re-running it with a few WikiText eval sentences may be the cheapest first check. **3. Decon would have missed torch-nplm even with Paloma indexed** Paloma isn't in the decon eval corpus, and `wikitext` is excluded on purpose (`DECON_EXCLUDED_EVAL_TASKS`, #6852 cluster A). I indexed the PTB validation text (Paloma's `ptb`) anyway to test the matcher. I ran the matching functions in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/decon.py` unchanged, using the `reference_pipeline.py` settings: 13-grams, overlap ≥ 0.5, ≥ 2 matched features, paragraphs split on `\n\n`. When most lines of a paragraph are windows that shift by one token, stitch them back into running text, drop ``, and score the result as an extra paragraph. Overlap goes back to 1.000. In 5,724 ordinary code and text files (the Marin repo and the CPython 3.12 standard library), the pass triggered on none of 241,449 paragraphs. Details are on #6852, the issue about this matcher's recall. So one store-wide pass may be cheaper than scanning step ranges. Run decon in flag-only mode against Paloma `ptb` and `wikitext_103`, with the stitching pass, and then run `find_doc_steps.py` on what it flags. Raw copies would score about 1.0. **4. The 7 Uncheatable subsets show no drops at any threshold I tried, which fits #9729. A follow-up on the store-wide pass from (3). I ran a narrower check: a 13-gram scan of the public Stack v3, the source of the torch-nplm document, limited to files whose path or size looks like PTB or WikiText data. Apart from torch-nplm, none of them holds either validation text. So the other drops, at 104,999 and 191,999 for PTB and the WikiText ones, still need your scanner or a store-wide pass.

**Scope**

| Eval text | Best file in Stack v3 | Share of the eval's 13-grams |
|---|---|---|
| PTB valid (Paloma `ptb` val) | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/valid.6grams` | 0.988, de-windowed |
| PTB test | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/test.6grams` | 0.987, de-windowed |

None of the standard `ptb.*.txt` files is in stack-v3-train, and no selected file outside torch-nplm shares a single 13-gram with the validation text, as written or de-windowed. So the other copy I guessed at in (1) isn't in a Stack v3 file that looks like PTB data.

topics.title: [levanter] Shift eval targets across context shards
topics.body:
Use the sharding-aware next-token shift from the training loss in tagged and labeled LM evaluation. An explicitly sharded context axis previously made JAX reject the evaluator's position roll before held-out metrics were emitted.

Preserve the explicit token layout for byte lookup when context is sharded. On a two-device CPU mesh, tagged evaluation matches unsharded loss and bits-per-byte metrics, and labeled evaluation returns the reference next-token IDs.

Fixes #10232
topics.head: 479875419f8857887c43e68d7beb65b21138b987

comments.body: Working on this in loom: https://loom.oa.dev/s/vchtjft4

topics.title: [levanter] LM evaluation fails with explicitly context-sharded tokens
topics.body:
Held-out LM evaluation fails when token positions are explicitly sharded across a context mesh. Training updates succeed; the first evaluation raises:

```text
lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py:238, _default_lm_eval_loss_fn
per_pos_token_id = jnp.roll(named_batch.tokens.array, -1, axis=-1)
ShardingTypeError: `a` cannot be sharded on the axis being rolled over.
Got arr type=i32[16@(replica_dcn,data,expert),32768@context] and axis=(1,)
```

Reproduce:
1. Use an explicit mesh with local axes `data=1, replica=1, model=1, expert=8` and inter-node axes `replica_dcn=1, context=4` (32 GPUs).
2. Map `batch` to `(replica_dcn,data,expert)` and `position` to `context`, with global batch 16 and sequence length 32,768.
3. Run `cb_tagged_lm_evaluate` on a model and batch with that layout. Its default loss callback reaches the failing roll.

Expected: target-token shifting and token-weighted evaluation agree with an unsharded reference. The training loss path in `models/loss.py` already gathers the token IDs along the sharded position axis before shifting and restores their layout afterward.

Observed in the #10213 sweep at completed update 548, its first held-out evaluation, on base commit `753bbb163c78f0e7ea50059522f42156708162c8` plus experiment-local changes. Iris job: `/karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft`. Retrieve the error with `uv run iris --cluster=marin task logs /karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft/1 --substring ShardingTypeError`.

The labeled callback contains the same roll at `eval.py:277`; that path was not exercised in this run. This issue tracks the shared evaluator fix separately from moving the sweep's validation offline.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Both default LM evaluation callbacks call `jnp.roll` on token arrays whose position axis may be explicitly sharded. JAX rejects that roll before the evaluator can aggregate loss or byte counts. The evaluator already receives the mesh mapping needed to restore the token layout after shifting.

**Relevant code**
- [`eval.py#L223-L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L223-L237) — tagged callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L259-L276`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L259-L276) — labeled callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L531-L577`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L531-L577) — token IDs feed byte aggregation

# Proposed Fix

`TaggedEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` or `LabeledEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` → default loss callback → `jnp.roll` on context-sharded positions → `ShardingTypeError`. Replicate the position axis for the shift, then restore its mapped sharding in both default callbacks; verify token IDs and token-weighted metrics against an unsharded reference on a small context mesh.

🤖 Fix is open in #10233. Both default callbacks use the training loss's sharding-safe token shift, and byte lookup keeps an explicit output layout for context shards. Two-device CPU regressions match unsharded tagged loss and bits-per-byte metrics and labeled next-token IDs; the focused evaluator and loss suite passed 23 tests. The full Levanter run hit an unrelated Grug MoE test that uses `ragged-all-to-all`, which XLA:CPU does not support; all-files Pyrefly reported missing optional imports outside the changed files.
🤖 PR #10233 passed CI, including the Levanter unit and repository lint jobs. It remains open and mergeable, with review required and no submitted reviews after the 12-hour monitor timeout.

topics.title: Weekly preemptible-compute accounting from Iris finelog → surface in MWS, attributed to users (and GitHub issues)
topics.body:
_Filed by an AI agent on behalf of **@penfever** (LAION / OpenThoughts), labeled `agent-generated` per the repo's [AI-generated contributions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/dev-guide/contributing.md) policy._

@rjpower — do you think we could surface some summary stats from **Iris finelog** that would let us track Marin **preemptible compute use weekly**, drop it into **MWS** as a summary section, and map it to **users** (certainly) and ideally to **public GitHub issues**? I think it would give everyone greater confidence about "where the compute is all going."

The motivation is transparency. "Where did the compute go this week?" currently gets answered anecdotally. A weekly, per-user (and ideally per-issue) rollup of preemptible TPU-hours — plus how much we lose to preemption churn — would give the team one shared, citable picture instead.

### Why this looks tractable today

Iris already carries most of the raw material:

- **Attribution is first-class.** Jobs carry `owner_principal` / `submitting_user` (controller.proto), and there's a `ListUsers` API — so per-user rollups don't need to parse names out of job paths.
- **Per-job compute + waste is already derivable from finelog job history.** `scripts/iris/analyze_job_history.py` paginates the full history and reports `total_runtime_s`, `iris_preemption_count`, per-cycle placement/serve, etc. Aggregate that across a week by user × cluster × accelerator and you get chip-hours plus a preemption-overhead figure.
- **Region / accelerator are on the placement**, so we can split v5p vs v6e and us-central1 vs us-east5 vs europe-west4.

### Proposed shape

1. A weekly job that reads finelog (or reuses the `analyze_job_history` aggregation) and emits, per ISO week:
   - preemptible TPU **chip-hours** by **user**, by **cluster/region**, by **accelerator type**;
   - a **preemption-overhead** metric — chip-hours (or wall-time) lost to preempt → re-place churn vs. productive compute. This is the "what are we actually paying for preemptible" number, and it's the one people are surprised by;
   - top-N jobs by chip-hours.
2. Drop a compact table into **MWS** each week (the same weekly-summary artifact the team already reads), so it shows up where people are already looking.
3. **Stretch — map to GitHub issues.** This is the one piece of glue that doesn't exist cleanly today. Users are easy (`owner_principal`); issues need a job → issue link — e.g. a launch-time convention (`issue=#NNNN` in job labels/metadata) or a maintained lookup. Worth deciding whether that's in scope for v1 or a follow-up.

### Open questions

- **Finelog retention** — is a full ISO-week of job/task events reliably inside the retention window, or do we need to snapshot the weekly aggregate before it ages out? (This probably decides whether the weekly job is "read finelog directly" vs. "roll up incrementally into a durable table.")
- **Preemptible vs. reserved** — preemptible-only, or report both with a split?
- **"Productive vs. wasted" definition** — do cold-compile / resume-scan chip-hours count as overhead, or only the re-placement gaps between attempts?
- **Attribution granularity** — user-level for v1 with issue-level as a fast-follow, or hold for the issue link?

Happy to prototype the finelog → weekly-aggregate step if the shape sounds right — the per-job pieces are already there in `analyze_job_history`; the new parts are the weekly grouping, the overhead metric, and the MWS drop.

🤖 Scoped and published as a design PR: #7387 (`design.md` / `research.md` / `spec.md` under `.agents/projects/iris_compute_accounting/`). Ran the codex peer review you asked for, plus a fable and an architect pass — they found two load-bearing things that reshaped the doc.

**On your "iris event `<started/preempted/resumed/finished> <user> <time> <resources>`" intuition** — that's exactly the missing piece and it's the core of the proposal: a durable `iris.accounting` finelog namespace, one row per terminated attempt. Zone/region/preemptible live on the `workers` row, and `remove_worker` deletes that row and NULLs `task_attempts.worker_id` in the *same transaction* that terminalizes a preempted attempt (`writes.py:734`) — so a post-hoc query sees NULL placement for the entire preemption cohort at t=0, and `worker_retention` is only 24h anyway. (`iris.task_event` is a same-named red herring: k8s scheduling verdicts, ~1h retention.) So there's no "just query finelog weekly" shortcut for the preemptible split — the emit is the work.

**On prometheus MFU** — good news: MFU-per-job is *already* durable in the finelog `telltale` namespace (`levanter_throughput_mfu`), and Grafana already reads it. Two caveats: it's Levanter-training-only (vLLM/Zephyr emit nothing), and TPUs have **no** hardware duty-cycle telemetry at all, so for TPUs MFU is the only "are the chips busy" signal. "Downtime" needs the same terminalization capture (recovery-idle = gap between a preempted attempt finishing and the next starting).

**One honesty flag on the headline number:** "chip-hours lost to preemption" as full preempted-attempt runtime is a large over-count — Levanter checkpoints and resumes, and user cancels land as KILLED-with-started rows. The doc reports a labeled *upper bound* plus a separately-computed recovery-idle figure instead.

Genuinely-your-call Open Questions (in `design.md`): the emit's delivery guarantee (best-effort + reconciliation vs. transactional outbox), where the `MARIN_ISSUE` number comes from, and whether to measure attribution coverage (how much compute is `local_admin` vs. a real email) before building. I can start Phase 0 — the cheap attribution-coverage probe — while the design gets eyes.

🤖 Fair hit — the first draft described joins without the queries. I went and ran them against live finelog (DuckDB over the GCS parquet), so these are real numbers, and rewrote the spec query-first. Pushed to #7387.

**How you find MFU for a job.** Levanter already forwards `throughput/mfu` to the durable finelog `telltale` namespace as `levanter_throughput_mfu`, tagged with `job_id` (iris root) and `run` (wandb). Two gotchas the real data exposed that the abstract version got wrong: `process_index` is NULL (so my "dedup to process 0" returned nothing), and on a multislice job every worker forwards the same value — so collapse per step first:

```sql
WITH per_step AS (
  SELECT job_id, run, ts, any_value(value) AS mfu
  FROM "telltale"
  WHERE name='levanter_throughput_mfu' AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}
  GROUP BY job_id, run, ts)
SELECT job_id, run, round(avg(mfu),1) AS mean_mfu, count(*) steps
FROM per_step GROUP BY job_id, run ORDER BY steps DESC;
```

Real output right now:
```
/runner/iris-run-job-20260718-074819   canary-tpu-...          19.1   139
/runner/iris-run-job-20260718-113025   grug-multislice-smoke   4.5      9
```
(`_mean_mfu`, `_p10/50/90_mfu` are forwarded too, so percentiles are free.)

**What other queries.** Two more run today with no new infra — full SQL + real output in [spec.md §1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/issue-7353/.agents/projects/iris_compute_accounting/spec.md):
- Preemptions by pool/zone from `iris.provisioning` — last 7d: v6e-4/us-east1-d **471**, v5p-8/us-east5-a **311**.
- Host-hours by user from `iris.task` (its `task_id` is `/user/job/...`, so `split_part(task_id,'/',2)` is the user) — last 24h: eczech **21.6h**, larry **12.4h**, michaelryan **4.7h**.

So Phase 1 is a real report on existing finelog. The one thing finelog can't give is **chip-hours** (iris.task has no device count) or the **preemptible/region split** (that placement is deleted from the DB the instant a preempted attempt terminates — `remove_worker`, `writes.py:734`, 24h worker retention). That's the only reason for the new `iris.accounting` row in Phase 2.

**The dashboard.** `infra/grafana/dashboards/compute.json` — each panel is one of these finelog-SQL queries through the existing bridge. Phase-1 panels (MFU/job, preemptions/pool, host-hours/user) render immediately; the chip-hours/waste panels turn on when `iris.accounting` lands, no dashboard change. Panel table in spec.md §4.

Want me to just build Phase 1 (the report + a couple of Grafana panels off what's live today) so you can see it running, and keep `iris.accounting` as the follow-up?

🤖 Done — one combined PR (#7387): design docs + a working `scripts/ops/compute_report.py` + unit tests + a weekly cron, verified end-to-end against live finelog.

**The planned iris.accounting controller emit turned out to be unnecessary.** Once I queried the live data instead of the schema, the placement I thought was destroyed at preemption is right there in the `iris.task` `worker_id` string:

```
marin-tpu-v5p-preemptible-32-us-east5-a-...-worker-1
         └gen  └capacity    └chips └zone           └host
```

`iris.task` retains that durably in finelog, so chip-hours + the preemptible/reserved split need **no controller change** — the review's "placement is deleted when a preempted attempt terminates" was about the controller DB's `workers` row, but the same facts live in the durable `iris.task` namespace. Per-host chips = a slice's chips over its live hosts (SPMD → every host emits rows); chip-hours = host active-seconds × chips-per-host.

**Real output, 2026-W29** (aggregates; the per-user table is in the report the cron gists to Discord):

| capacity | generation | chip-hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reserved | v4 | 155,573 |
| preemptible | v5p | 67,614 |
| preemptible | v6e | 44,399 |
| preemptible | v5e | 20,282 |

Totals: **132,659 preemptible + 155,573 reserved chip-hours**, 96% of active worker-time on parseable TPU workers. Plus 2,036 preemption events (led by v6e-4/us-east1-d), and MFU per job (canary run 19.1%).

The one thing `iris.task` doesn't carry is per-attempt terminal cause, so "chip-hours *lost* to preemption" (vs consumed on preemptible capacity) is the remaining follow-up — either a controller SELECT within the 7-day retention window, or a tiny terminal-cause emit. I left `iris.accounting` out entirely since it's no longer load-bearing.
