topics.title: [grug] Publish Snowball (67B-A2B 2T cooldown) to Hugging Face
topics.body:
## Description

Publish the "Snowball" checkpoint — the Grug 67B-A2B intermediate cooldown trained on 2T tokens (of 10T) in #6811 — to Hugging Face so external users can try it. The hero run has landed and SFT/midtraining, chat templating, vLLM serving, and evals are green (announced 2026-07-17). Publishing was agreed in the #6811 thread: @hammer asked, @ClassicLarry and @yonromai concurred, with prerequisites noted below.

Final permanent checkpoint (Levanter/Grug format):
`gs://marin-us-central2/grug/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k-79ebf3/checkpoints/step-42150/`
(567 objects, ~539 GB; note step-**42150**, not 42149 — see https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811#issuecomment-4952891213 correction by @yonromai). Regional mirrors already exist in `s3://marin-us-east-02a/...` and `gs://marin-us-east5/...`.

Prerequisites raised in the thread, which this task must resolve first:
- **Standardize the config against HF conventions** before export (@ClassicLarry).
- **Serialization contract for external use.** A Grug→safetensors export exists in `main` but was written for internal vLLM serving; it needs hardening for external consumers (@yonromai).
- **Inference-path caveat.** Grug is only runnable today via Levanter/JAX or the Marin vLLM fork (https://github.com/marin-community/vllm); upstream vLLM/transformers does not support the architecture. The HF model card must document this so external users know how to load it.

### Definition of Done

- Grug step-42150 checkpoint exported to safetensors with an HF-standard config, uploaded to a `marin-community` HF repo.
- Model card documents architecture (67B total / ~2B active MoE, d2560, 2T-token cooldown), provenance (links #6811), license, and the supported inference paths (Marin vLLM fork / Levanter), with a working load-and-generate snippet.
- Exported weights verified to produce outputs matching the source checkpoint under the Marin vLLM fork.

Parent hero run: #6811.

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Actionability check — issue is actionable (clear DoD) but large (release + export infra, ~539 GB, HF upload, model card, parity verification). Per fix-issue scoping this warrants analysis, **not** a PR.
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight — no open PRs/issues for grug safetensors export or Snowball publish.
- [x] Locate existing export machinery and config mapping.
- [ ] Human review of the approach below before implementation.

# Research

A working Grug→safetensors export already exists, but it lives **inside the vLLM E2E test harness**, is wired to a fixed region, and uses an internal-serving weight layout — exactly the three prerequisites the #6811 thread flagged (HF-standard config, external serialization contract, documented inference path).

- The export itself is one `converter.save_pretrained(...)` call, sharded into 256 MB safetensors, buried in a test backend: [`grugmoe_real_checkpoint_backend.py#L362-L427`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/tests/vllm/grugmoe_real_checkpoint_backend.py#L362-L427).
- It exports via a **legacy split-expert** state-dict layout, not the canonical `grugmoe_inference_state_dict`: [`#L266`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/tests/vllm/grugmoe_real_checkpoint_backend.py#L266) vs [`model.py#L862`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L862) — this is the "which layout do external consumers get" contract to pin down.
- `to_hf_config()` emits **dual grug+HF field names** (`hidden_dim`+`hidden_size`, `num_experts`+`num_local_experts`, …) plus a private `grug_moe_artifact_schema_version` — this is the non-standard config @ClassicLarry wants normalized: [`model.py#L228-L265`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L228-L265).
- Region lock: the harness hard-requires `europe-west4` for every path ([`#L129`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/tests/vllm/grugmoe_real_checkpoint_backend.py#L129)); the checkpoint is in `us-central2` (mirrors `us-east5` / `s3://marin-us-east-02a`). Reading 539 GB cross-region violates the AGENTS.md cost rule — export must run co-located with a mirror.
- HF push is already supported by the converter: `save_pretrained(..., upload_to_hf=RepoRef)` creates the repo and uploads: [`hf_checkpoints.py#L1027-L1137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L1027-L1137). No model-card generation exists — the README must be authored and uploaded separately.

# Proposed Approach (for review — not yet implemented)

Extract the export from the test harness into a reusable, region-parameterized CLI (e.g. `experiments/grug/moe/export_to_hf.py`) and run it as a one-off release job co-located with a checkpoint mirror:

1. **Pin the serialization contract.** Decide canonical layout: reuse `grugmoe_inference_state_dict` (matches the Marin vLLM fork loader) vs the legacy split-expert layout the harness currently ships. Document tensor naming so the fork + Levanter both round-trip. This is the core "harden for external use" work.
2. **Standardize `config.json`.** Choose HF-canonical keys as authoritative (`hidden_size`, `num_local_experts`, `num_experts_per_tok`, `rms_norm_eps`, `num_hidden_layers`, …); keep the grug aliases only if the fork loader still reads them, otherwise drop them. Keep `architectures: ["GrugMoeForCausalLM"]` and the schema-version key.
3. **Region.** Run the export on a worker in `us-east5` (or `us-central2`) reading the local mirror; write the safetensors output to the same region, then upload to HF. No cross-region 539 GB reads.
4. **Upload** to `marin-community/<name>` via `save_pretrained(upload_to_hf=...)`, `private=True` first.
5. **Model card.** Author `README.md`: architecture (67B total / ~2B active MoE, d2560, 2T-of-10T cooldown, step-**42150**), provenance (link #6811), license, supported inference paths (Marin vLLM fork / Levanter — upstream vLLM/transformers unsupported), and a working load-and-generate snippet. Upload alongside weights.
6. **Verify parity.** Reuse the existing E2E vLLM parity check ([`test_grugmoe_real_checkpoint_e2e.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/tests/vllm/test_grugmoe_real_checkpoint_e2e.py)) against the exported repo under the Marin fork to satisfy the DoD's "outputs match source checkpoint".

**Open questions for a human before I proceed:**
- Target HF repo name under `marin-community`, and license to declare.
- Canonical weight layout: `grugmoe_inference_state_dict` or the legacy split-expert layout the fork currently expects?
- Which region/machine to run the ~539 GB export on (TPU vs CPU worker; co-located mirror).
- Keep or drop the dual grug/HF config aliases (depends on the fork loader).

Given the scope (checkpoint-export infra + a large one-off release job, not a code bugfix), I'm stopping here for review rather than opening a PR.

topics.title: [tpu] Step12 TPU serving diverges from H100 past the 2048-token sliding window
topics.body:
On TPU, Snowball Step12 assigns different next-token log probabilities than H100 from token position 2048 onward. Up to position 2047 the two platforms agree to within TPU run-to-run noise. Step12 uses `sliding_window = 2048` with `global_every = 4`, so three of every four attention layers attend only to the last 2048 tokens. The divergence starts at that window size.

Impact: MATH500 on the same model, revision and Evalchemy commit scores 0.944 and 0.950 on H100 and 0.878, 0.882 (v6e-8, TP8) and 0.884 (v5p-8, TP4) on TPU. 39 items are correct on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU; 22 of them are long answers that drift to a different question.

Measurement: teacher-forced log probabilities of the same 10 texts on each platform (rendered Step12 chat prefix plus an H100-generated, H100-correct MATH500 completion; vLLM `/v1/completions` with `echo`, `logprobs=1`, `max_tokens=0`, concurrency 1). 35,801 scored positions; token ids are identical on both platforms.

| Positions | H100 vs TPU mean \|Δlogprob\| | top-1 token differs | TPU concurrency 1 vs 10 mean \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.010–0.019 | 0.8–1.0% | 0.012–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.026 | 1.6% | – |
| 2368–2559 | 0.066 | 3.1–3.3% | – |
| 2048–3071 | 0.063 | 3.6% | 0.014 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.142 | 6.8% | 0.018 |

Pooled over all positions: mean \|Δ\| 0.056 (TPU self-noise 0.014), maximum 12.3 (TPU self-noise 1.1), top-1 differs at 2.8% of positions (TPU self-noise 0.86%). TPU's mean per-token negative log likelihood is higher on all 10 items.

The per-element window mask agrees across the three stacks. Each keeps the last W tokens including the query token:
- training: [`levanter/grug/attention/_core.py` L126](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py#L123-L126), `k >= q - (W - 1)`;
- H100 vLLM fork: [`grugmoe.py` L957-L964](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py#L957-L964) passes `per_layer_sliding_window=2048` on local layers;
- TPU: [`grugmoe.py` L786](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L776-L787) passes the window as `attention_chunk_size`, which [`attention_interface.py` L496](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L494-L498) forwards as `sliding_window`; the RPA v3 kernel masks with [`q < k + W` at L494](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494).

The cause is not confirmed. Two unverified suspects on the TPU path:
- the RPA v3 sliding-window block skipping, which computes the first KV block to read from `kv_q_gap - sliding_window` ([kernel.py L388-L399](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399), [L916-L942](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942));
- KV-cache handling for the sliding-window layers.

Reproduce:
1. Serve `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` at revision `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`, bf16. TPU: v6e-8, TP8, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d`, vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`. H100: H100x8, DP8 with expert parallelism, Marin vLLM fork build `01911be34fac`.
2. Run `python teacher_forced_logprobs.py --endpoint URL --model open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 --items teacher_forced_items.json --output DIR --concurrency 1` against each server. The client and items (sha256 `9d4779361b79259d36dcd2402d6fe686c81884d111cab550bb6c7fff158cdc4d`) are in `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/inputs/`.
3. Compare with `python compare_tf.py H100_DIR/results.json TPU_DIR/results.json` from the same folder, and bin `|Δlogprob|` by position.

Expected: TPU per-position log probabilities stay within TPU run-to-run noise of H100 at every position, including beyond 2048.

Next step: rerun the TPU side with `grugmoe_attention_mode` set to the dense reference path (`_dense_reference_attention` in `grugmoe.py`, which applies the window as an explicit mask). If dense-mode TPU matches H100 past position 2048, the defect is in the production RPA path.

Caveats: the H100 completions were re-tokenized from text because the eval record has no sampled token ids, and vLLM omits special tokens such as the leading `<|start_think|>` from returned text. Both platforms scored the same bytes, so the comparison is valid, but the first completion positions are not a replay of the original sampled trajectory.

Data:
- H100: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-h100x8/concurrency-1/`
- TPU v6e-8: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-v6e8/concurrency-{1,10}/`
- H100 MATH500 per-item and three-way tables: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task224-math500/`

comments.body:
🤖 Correction to the next step in the description: a config-only dense-mode rerun is not available on the serving path.

- The served vLLM build (`fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`) never reads `grugmoe_attention_mode`; its Grug model always uses the `Attention` layer (`vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py` L958-L964). Passing the field through `hf_overrides` changes nothing.
- The dense switch exists only in tpu-inference's reference JAX model ([`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py` L233, L738-L804](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L738-L804)). That class is not in the JAX model registry used for serving, and its dense path ignores the KV cache.

The replacement control is a kernel-level test: run tpu-inference's ragged paged attention tests with Step12's shapes (sliding window 2048, page size 16, 32 query / 8 KV heads after padding) against the reference implementation on a v6e-4.

🤖
# Research

The 2048-token onset implicates local attention, but matching elementwise mask inequalities do not establish that TPU RPA visits the right KV blocks or reads intact cache pages. `GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` selects a dense path that computes from the full input without updating KV cache, or a production path that calls RPA v3. The measured TPU revision is the head of [tpu-inference#27](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/27); [marin#9400](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400) qualifies a June checkpoint, not Step12.

**Relevant code**
- [`grugmoe.py#L738-L805`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L738-L805) — dense and production attention paths
- [`attention_interface.py#L493-L510`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L493-L510) — window forwarded to RPA
- [`kernel.py#L388-L399`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399) — first KV block selection
- [`kernel.py#L493-L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494) — elementwise window mask
- [`kernel.py#L916-L942`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942) — per-query-block traversal

# Proposed Fix

`GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` → `shared_attention()` → RPA v3 is the production call chain. The failing step within that chain is not established, so use the frozen Step12 inputs to isolate it:

1. Replay the issue's 10 teacher-forced inputs on the reported TPU revisions with `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` and `production`; force one complete prefill per request because dense has no historical KV-cache reads, verify identical token IDs, and compare bins around position 2048 with the existing H100 results.
2. If dense agrees with H100, compare RPA v3 with a dense QKV reference at positions 2047, 2048, 2111, and 3072 across page and query-block boundaries, including full prefill, chunked prefill, decode, skipped KV blocks, and cache/page-table contents; otherwise find the first divergent layer output and compare its Q/K/V, RoPE, mask, and loaded weights with Levanter.
3. Fix the identified TPU fork path, add a regression across position 2048, rerun the frozen log-probability comparison and repeated MATH500 on the same checkpoint, and coordinate with the open `tpu-inference#27` stack before updating Marin's paired fork pin; the post-window H100–TPU error should return to measured TPU run-to-run noise before hardware qualification.

topics.title: Experiment: TransformerEngine NCCL_EP expert-parallel MoE on B200
topics.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment evaluated whether TransformerEngine NCCL_EP could replace or beat Marin's incumbent `a2a_cute` expert-parallel MoE path on GB200/B200 systems. The core goal was met: TE/NCCL_EP builds, imports, and trains at 64 GPUs with EP8, with loss parity and near-parity throughput. A custom NCCL_EP transport seam plus MoE-layer chunking made the production b1024 x seq4096 d5120 L48 case train at 18.0% MFU versus 19.1% for `a2a_cute`, and chunk rematerialization removed the no-drop EP capacity wall by making peak EP memory scale with one chunk rather than full batch/seqlen. The later fairness and gap-closing work found that TE's full `moe()` block performs about the same as the custom seam but remains around 1.1-1.3 percentage points behind `a2a_cute`; command-buffer scoping, collective-overlap flags, and `max_num_sms` tuning were wash-or-loss in bf16. The current recommendation is to keep `a2a_cute` as the incumbent for bf16, preserve NCCL_EP/chunking as a derisked path, and next pursue NVIDIA/TE follow-ups: report the TE main-tip 64-GPU regression, test quantized fp8/MXFP8 support when available, and revisit NGC-stack arms after the compile stall is understood.

### Helpful links
- Full logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md
- 64-GPU EP8 goal gate: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5008121573
- Production b1024 chunking result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5009585521
- Full TE MoE block benchmark: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5073227834
- Gap-closing benchmark and TE tip regression: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7331#issuecomment-5076118699
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

NVIDIA's recommendations for EP MoE on JAX/XLA GPU (2026-07-13/14):

1. `jax.ragged_dot` was made performant in NGC JAX 26.05 (`xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion=ON`, confirmed supported on B200).
2. TransformerEngine has a MoE block backed by NCCL_EP ([TE #3036](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3036), C API in [TE #3034](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3034)) — "equivalent to DeepEP/HybridEP with no external dependency". The 8k-seq-len staging limit (which caps local batch size at 2) is actively being removed.
3. The JAX MoE speed-of-light solution will require TransformerEngine as the time-to-market way to expose NCCL_EP.

The full TE MoE block (router/permute, hybridEP A2A, grouped GEMMs) lives on the WIP branch [`jberchtold/teddy-te-ep-integration-2026-07-08-support-quantization`](https://github.com/jberchtold-nvidia/TransformerEngine/blob/jberchtold/teddy-te-ep-integration-2026-07-08-support-quantization/transformer_engine/jax/moe.py), targeted for merge into TE main. Early external testing of that branch is reportedly promising.

Prior state on our side (#7012 / #7279): hypothesis H-te is Blocked in the [7012 logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7012-b200-mfu/.agents/logbooks/7012-b200-moe-mfu.md) — a 2026-07-15 API probe found TE 2.15.0+42b840051 ships `grouped_dense`/`permutation`/`router` but no NCCL_EP JAX surface. A source read of the TE PRs noted: 8192-token `max_tokens_per_rank` staging default, bf16-only dispatch wire (fp8 wire on the quantization WIP branch), one-sided `max_num_sms`, process-per-GPU requirement, and that it disables NCCL comm-splitting and command-buffer capture. #7279's hypothesis queue already ranks the NCCL_EP-style chunked-pipeline decomposition #1 by expected value.

## Hypothesis or Goal

NCCL_EP's SM-capped persistent comm kernels feeding chunked expert GEMMs beat our current EP legs in the latency-bound NVL72 regime. Concretely:

1. Build TE from the WIP branch on the B200 container stack and get the JAX MoE block importable.
2. Microbench dispatch/combine vs our measured baselines: XLA `ragged_all_to_all` one-shot kernel pathology (~297 ms/call, B200MFU-018) and the NCCL fallback (one-shot kernel disabled, B200MFU-025).
3. If the microbench wins, e2e MFU comparison at the canonical d2560 MoE config vs the current best (ring_cute EP4, 20.83% at 64 GPUs, #7279).
4. Assess the fp8/MXFP8 dispatch-wire path as the follow-on (dispatch bytes halve; ties into the MXFP8 work in #7282).

Caveat from prior evidence: SM-capping alone was falsified twice on this stack (B200MFU-016, B200MFU-021) — the value, if any, is in the chunked-pipeline decomposition and the fused dispatch, not the SM budget.

## Status

Goal met for build/import/train and production-shape derisking. NCCL_EP is not currently recommended as the bf16 default over `a2a_cute`: the best TE-backed arms remain about 1.3 percentage points behind `a2a_cute`, and the latest TE main tip regresses at the full 64-GPU data8 x expert8 topology. Next steps are NVIDIA escalation for that regression, quantized fp8/MXFP8 wire when TE exposes it, and NGC-stack retests after the compile stall is understood.

## Links

* Logbook: [.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md) (branch `research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep`)
* W&B Report:
* Important updates: prior context in #7012 (H-te) and #7279 (hypothesis queue)

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.body:
🤖 NCCLEP-001 (source read): the dependency chain is **fully public** — no closed libnccl_ep artifact.

- TE PRs #3034 (C API + NCCL EP backend) and #3036 (JAX `ep_dispatch`/`ep_combine` primitives + VJPs) are **merged into TE main** (June 13/27); the WIP branch is only needed later for the fp8 dispatch wire. The negative 2026-07-15 probe is explained: that wheel predates the JAX merge.
- `libnccl_ep.a` builds from the in-tree `3rdparty/nccl` submodule pinned to public NVIDIA/nccl `b87848fbc` (v2.30u1 line) and links statically; `NVTE_WITH_NCCL_EP=ON` is the TE build default.
- Runtime gate: system NCCL >= 2.30.4 (our stack runs 2.28.9; PyPI `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` has aarch64 wheels).
- Contract at the merged surface: process-per-GPU (`local_device_count()==1`), bf16-only wire, TE MeshResource ep axis, num_experts % ep_size == 0. Staging math at the reference config (65,536 tokens/rank): zero-drop recv capacity at EP8 is ~21.4 GiB/rank — sizing to expected load × margin is one of the at-scale questions this issue exists to answer.

Next: build TE main (tip `68493d2d`) inside the NGC container on a GB200 node, import-probe the `te.jax.ep` surface (NCCLEP-002). Details in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md).

🤖 NCCLEP-002: **TE + NCCL_EP builds and imports on the goal platform.**

Wheel `transformer_engine-2.18.0.dev0+68493d2` (TE main, sm_100a, arm64) built natively on a GB200 iris pod with a synthetic CUDA_HOME assembled from pip cu13 wheels — no container. Import probe under **stock jax 0.10.1** on 4×GB200 shows the full `te.jax.ep` surface (`ep_bootstrap`/`ep_dispatch`/`ep_combine`); runtime NCCL upgraded to 2.30.7 (EP gate is >= 2.30.4). Wheel is stashed in object storage; build recipe is `experiments/ncclep/build_te_wheel.sh` on the research branch (11 attempts; the gotcha list is in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md)).

One design constraint surfaced by source read: TE EP supports a **single** dp/fsdp axis outside `ep`, so the replica-2 × 32-GPU-copy reference layout won't bootstrap as-is — the first 64-GPU EP8 target will be a single-copy data8×expert8 mesh (still ≥32-way sharded); replica-DP-outside is worth reporting upstream.

In flight: single-node 4-proc TE EP test-suite smoke, then EP4 / cross-node EP8 transport microbenches.

🤖 NCCLEP-003: **NCCL_EP is running on our stack** — TE's full multi-process EP test suite passes (13/13 in 17.7 s) on 4×GB200, one process per GPU: bootstrap, dispatch/combine primitive round trips, custom_vjp gradient closed-form checks, and the HLO guard that no XLA collectives leak around the EP FFI ops.

Two runtime discoveries on the way (fixes in `experiments/ncclep/` on the research branch):
- The gpu venv's cu12 wheels (torch deps) leaked into the first build's link (`libcublas.so.12` soname mismatch) — the toolchain merge is now cu13-only and the smoke asserts TE core's DT_NEEDED is clean.
- **NCCL_EP JIT-compiles its device kernels at bootstrap** via an external nvcc: every rank needs nvcc + CUDA headers + the generated `nccl_ep` JIT header tree at runtime (none packaged in the wheel). The build job now stashes the headers; launchers set `NCCL_EP_JIT_*` env.

In flight: transport microbenches at reference shapes (65,536 tokens/rank × hidden 5120 × top-4) — EP4 single-node and EP8 across 2 nodes (first cross-node NCCL_EP over MNNVL). Details in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md).

🤖 NCCLEP-005: **NCCL_EP trains end-to-end in the standalone MFU bench with loss parity.**

New `--moe-implementation nccl_ep` backend on branch `mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep-ncclep`: TE `ep_dispatch` → shard_map(QuACK grouped FFN via the `expert_mlp_fn` seam) → weighted hadamard → TE `ep_combine`, mirroring TE's own MoE block. Single-node EP4 smoke (d2560 L4 b16, process-per-GPU) vs a ring_cute control at the identical config: **step-0 loss bit-identical** (11.805191040039062), full 6-step trajectory parity to ~2e-5.

Notable integration findings (details in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md)):
- Command-buffer capture must be off around the EP FFI ops (TE's pointer-keyed handle cache), with `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=-1` — TE's own documented JAX workaround.
- **NCCL_EP has no drop path**: recv overflow is an OOB write that poisons the CUDA context, so capacity must be provisioned for the no-drop worst case (`ep × tokens × top_k` ≈ 21.5 GiB/rank at the reference config) — sub-worst-case capacity needs TE-side drop support (worth an upstream ask).
- The capacity tail of the dispatch buffer is uninitialized; grouped-GEMM wgrads over garbage rows NaN'd training until the tail was zeroed + the combine weighting switched from 0-mask multiply to `where`.
- TE's sharding rules assume auto-sharding meshes — the EP region runs under `jax.sharding.auto_axes` inside our explicit-sharding bench.

In flight (NCCLEP-006, the goal gate): 64-GPU **EP8** at the reference config (d5120 L48 e64 top4 b1024 seq4096; single-copy data8×expert8 per TE's single-outer-axis constraint) + an a2a_cute EP8 control at the identical mesh and flags.

🤖 NCCLEP-006: **Goal met — NCCL_EP trains at 64 GPUs with EP8 at a production-shape config, at parity loss and near-parity MFU with the incumbent EP backend.**

All arms: d5120 L48 e64 top4 seq4096, EP8, single 64-GPU model copy (data8×expert8; TE's single-outer-axis constraint), 16-node GB200 gang, one process per GPU, EP groups spanning 2 nodes over MNNVL, recompute_all, 20 steps.

| arm | batch | steady MFU (B200 conv.) | s/step | tok/s | final loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a2a_cute EP8 (baseline) | 1024 | 19.1 % | 15.7 | 266 k | 8.746 |
| a2a_cute EP8 (control) | 512 | 18.1 % | 8.3 | 252 k | 8.762 |
| **nccl_ep EP8** (first pass) | 512 | 7.3 % | 20.4 | 103 k | **8.760** |
| **nccl_ep EP8** (+tail fix) | 512 | **16.7–17.1 %** | 8.9 | 233–240 k | **8.760** |

The tail fix: the QuACK expert-GEMM seam extended the last expert group across the entire no-drop capacity buffer, multiplying FFN work ~4× — skipping the extension (safe once real rows are `where`-selected before combine) recovered 7.3 % → ~17 %. The remaining ~1 pp gap to a2a_cute is untuned: command buffers are globally disabled (required around EP FFI ops; could be scoped), a redundant tail-zeroing pass remains, and `max_num_sms` is at auto.

Scale-derisk findings (the point of this issue):

1. **b1024 at EP8 does not fit**: NCCL_EP has no drop path, so recv capacity must cover the worst case, and worst-case capacity scales ∝ `EP degree × per-rank tokens`. At b1024/EP8 that is 2.1 M rows/rank → a 172 GiB temp arena → OOM. This is NVIDIA's "8k max_tokens_per_rank limits local batch to 2" wall seen from the other side — their intended shape is small per-dispatch chunks. Upstream asks: capacity-clipped dispatch with drop accounting, or the chunked-dispatch mode; on our side, MoE-layer chunking would unlock big batches.
2. **Cross-node EP works out of the box** on the NVL72 rack (EP groups span nodes over MNNVL; NCCL_EP treats the whole rack as one NVLink domain).
3. Every rank needs the **JIT toolchain at runtime** (nvcc + CUDA headers + the generated `nccl_ep` header tree) — NCCL_EP JIT-compiles its device kernels at first use; a disk cache makes this a one-time ~2 min cost per config.
4. TE EP supports **one dp/fsdp axis outside `ep`** — replica-DP outside an FSDP×EP copy (our reference layout) won't bootstrap; worth an upstream request.

Reproduction: branch `mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep-ncclep` (backend + bench wiring + launchers), wheel build recipe on `research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep` (`experiments/ncclep/`), full narrative in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md). Jobs: `/mwittmann/ncclep-64g-ep8-b512{,-q,-t2}`, controls `/mwittmann/ncclep-64g-a2a-{ctl,b512}`.

Ranked next steps: (1) scope command-buffer disablement to the EP ops (both arms currently pay for global-off); (2) drop the redundant tail-zeroing pass; (3) MoE-layer chunking to unlock b1024+ (also NVIDIA's intended usage and the H-te chunked-pipeline shape); (4) `max_num_sms` sweep; (5) fp8 dispatch wire from the TE quantization WIP branch (ties into #7282).

🤖 NCCLEP-007: **MoE-layer chunking prototyped and derisked at the production config — b1024×seq4096 at 64 GPUs/EP8 now trains** (`/mwittmann/ncclep-64g-ep8-b1024-ck8k-r5`, 20 steps, first attempt):

| arm | batch | steady MFU (B200) | s/step | tok/s | final loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a2a_cute EP8 | 1024 | 19.1 % | 15.7 | 266 k | 8.7463 |
| **nccl_ep EP8, chunked C=8192** | 1024 | **18.0 %** | 16.6 | 252 k | **8.7450** |
| nccl_ep EP8, unchunked (prior) | 512 | 16.7–17.1 % | 8.9 | 233–240 k | 8.7598 |

The backend now splits each rank's token stream into fixed C-token chunks and `lax.scan`s dispatch → grouped FFN → combine per chunk, with **`jax.checkpoint` on the chunk body**. Both halves matter:

1. **Chunked dispatch** shrinks the TE staging + no-drop recv capacity to `ep × C × top_k` rows per dispatch (2.6 GiB at C=8192 vs 21.5 GiB monolithic).
2. **Chunk remat** is what actually clears the memory wall: without it, `scan` saves every chunk's capacity-sized tensors as backward residuals, and `K × (ep × C × top_k) = ep × T_local × top_k` — invariant of chunk size, i.e. the same ~165 GiB as the unchunked wall. A one-allocation discriminator job (a2a control PASS + three chunk sizes FAIL, one with an honest 164.93 GiB OOM) exposed this; with the checkpoint, backward recomputes one chunk at a time and peak EP memory is a single chunk's working set.

Consequence for scale derisk: **EP-side memory is now O(chunk), independent of batch and seqlen** — the "8k max_tokens_per_rank limits local batch" wall is fully gone on our side. Numerics are a pure token partition: step-0 loss bit-identical to unchunked; the loss edge over a2a_cute (8.745 vs 8.746) is consistent with no-drop vs cf-1.0 drops. Chunking costs nothing measurable in throughput (b1024-chunked 18.0 % ≥ b512-unchunked 17.1 %), leaving the same ~1 pp untuned gap to a2a_cute as before (command buffers globally off, redundant tail-zeroing, `max_num_sms` at auto, no chunk pipelining yet).

Remaining b1024-scale caveat, not nccl_ep-specific: the intermittent `cuModuleLoadData` CUBIN failure (B200MFU-036 — environmental, hits a2a/ring identically, no known flag mitigation) cost several retries tonight; the launcher now runs sequential in-job attempts with a shared compile cache (~10 min warm retries), and r5 passed on attempt 1.

Reproduction: `mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep-ncclep` @ 203858818 (`--ep-chunk-tokens`, chunk remat, retry loop, `experiments/ncclep/run_arms_b1024.sh` discriminator); full narrative in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md) (NCCLEP-007). Next candidates unchanged from the ranked list, now with chunking as the substrate for the real prize: pipelined chunks (dispatch k+1 overlapping FFN k), command-buffer scoping, fp8 wire (#7282).

🤖 NCCLEP-008/-009: **fairness correction + full TE MoE block benchmark.**

**Correction to the NCCLEP-006 framing** (raised in the #oa-nvidia thread): every `nccl_ep` arm so far used TE's NCCL_EP `ep_dispatch`/`ep_combine` primitives around **our own** QuACK/SonicMoE expert GEMMs and our own QB router. That was a controlled transport swap — valid for the transport question, but not a test of NVIDIA's recommended configuration, which is TE's whole fused MoE block (`transformer_engine.jax.moe.moe`, TE #2912 + #3116: fused sigmoid+top-k router → NCCL_EP dispatch → grouped-quantize + grouped GEMMs → NCCL_EP combine, one custom_vjp). The block merged into TE main 2026-07-10, seven days before our wheel build, so the stashed 68493d2 wheel already ships it — `moe.py` is byte-identical to today's main tip.

**NCCLEP-009: benchmarked the recommended path.** New `te_moe` backend (branch `mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep-ncclep` @ 81fcd979a) hands the entire MoE layer to `moe()`; grug's routing tensors feed only the observational stats and the QB bias update. Router parity: TE's sigmoid path (bias-steered top-k without gradient, sum-normalized weights × scaling factor 2.5) is our QB router up to the bias landing in score space instead of logit space — single-node smoke step-0 loss is bit-identical to the nccl_ep arms. Same wheel, same stock-jax 0.10.1 stack, three arms in ONE 16-node allocation (`/mwittmann/ncclep-b512-arms`), d5120 L48 e64 top4 seq4096 **b512** EP8, 64 GPUs, single copy data8×expert8, 20 steps; steady = median over steps ≥ 8:

| arm | steady MFU (B200 conv.) | s/step | tok/s | final loss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a2a_cute EP8 (incumbent) | **18.28 %** | 8.21 | 256 k | 8.7617 |
| nccl_ep EP8 (TE transport + QuACK FFN) | 17.15 % | 8.75 | 240 k | 8.7598 |
| te_moe EP8 (full TE MoE block) | 16.94 % | 8.86 | 237 k | 8.7649 |

Takeaways:

1. **The full block ties the seam** (16.94 vs 17.15 %, within same-allocation step noise) — the "maybe our integration undersold NCCL_EP" hypothesis is answered. At this config the recommended path lands where our seam did, ~1.1–1.3 pp below a2a_cute, so the earlier conclusion survives the fairness correction, now with the recommended integration actually tested.
2. Corollary: our QuACK FFN ≈ TE's grouped GEMMs here (consistent with B200MFU-011) and the fused-router gain is negligible; the gap to a2a_cute sits in the EP transport/capacity structure, not expert compute.
3. Loss parity three ways; te_moe's +5e-3 final loss is consistent with the score-space bias placement.

Caveats that still favor a future TE arm: bf16 wire and bf16 grouped GEMMs only (fp8/MXFP8 quantizer sets are explicitly out of scope in today's `moe.py`, while NVIDIA's headline DeepSeek-v3 GB300 numbers ride the MXFP8 recipe); our wheel predates TE #3231 (EP dispatch/combine scheduled on XLA's collective stream, 2026-07-22) and #3226 (orthogonal-axes bootstrap — our replica-DP ask, 2026-07-23); stock jax rather than NGC JAX 26.05 (ragged-dot fusion, multi-stream collectives, host offloading); command buffers globally off in all three arms; `moe()` has no chunked-dispatch mode, so b1024 remains behind the no-drop capacity wall on the full block where our chunked seam trains at 18.0 % (NCCLEP-007).

Ranked next steps: (1) rebuild TE at main tip and rerun the TE arms (#3231 is a plausible real win); (2) fp8 wire + MXFP8 grouped quant when `moe.py` grows quantizer support (ties #7282); (3) an NGC JAX container arm to test the full deck stack; (4) upstream ask: chunked-dispatch mode in `moe()`.

Full narrative: [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md) (NCCLEP-008/-009).

🤖 NCCLEP-010: **gap-closure benchmark — every non-quantization NVIDIA recommendation applied, in bf16.** Follow-up to NCCLEP-009's caveat list: TE rebuilt at main tip (#3231 EP-on-collective-stream, #3226), command-buffer capture scoped instead of globally off, multi-stream collective overlap (`--xla_gpu_experimental_parallel_collective_overlap_limit=2`), an `ep_bootstrap max_num_sms` sweep, and the NGC 26.06 container arm. Two findings:

**1. TE main tip (ea41e08, 2026-07-24) is a regression on our topology.** Both TE integrations — the full `moe()` block and the bare `ep_dispatch`/`ep_combine` seam — deterministically die at first 64-GPU execution at data8×expert8 (`ncclCommSplit ... remote process exited`, gang-wide coordination-service SIGABRT; 2/2 attempts × 4 arms across two allocations; no CUBIN signature). 2-node (data1×expert8) and 4-node (data2×expert8) topologies pass, so the trigger needs the full subgroup-clique structure. An import-time shim stripping #3231's `compute_on("gpu_stream:collective")` pin does NOT fix it, which exonerates the stream annotation as sole cause and points at the NCCL_EP relocation to the new `3rdparty/nccl-extensions` submodule (2c6135a, a different nccl_ep code line than the in-tree `NVIDIA/nccl@b87848f` our 68493d2 wheel used). Worth raising in #oa-nvidia: this blocks validating exactly the EP-overlap work (#3231) NVIDIA shipped this week.

**2. On the wheel that trains (68493d2), every knob is a wash or a loss.** One 16-node allocation (`/mwittmann/ncclep-gapclose3-arms`), d5120 L48 e64 top4 seq4096 b512 EP8, steady = median over steps ≥ 8; a2a-tuned from the sibling allocation (`ncclep-gapclose-arms`, anchor 18.24 %):

| arm | steady MFU | s/step | final loss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a2a_cute base | **18.24 %** | 8.23 | 8.7617 |
| a2a_cute tuned (default capture + overlap) | 18.19 % | 8.25 | 8.7616 |
| a2a_cute anchor (alloc 3) | 18.10 % | 8.29 | 8.7616 |
| nccl_ep seam + scoped capture + overlap | 17.15 % | 8.75 | 8.7598 |
| te_moe base | 16.82 % | 8.92 | 8.7649 |
| te_moe + scoped capture | 16.85 % | 8.90 | 8.7649 |
| te_moe + scoped capture + overlap | 16.78 % | 8.94 | 8.7649 |
| te_moe + … + max_num_sms 32 | 16.42 % | 9.13 | 8.7649 |
| te_moe + … + max_num_sms 16 | 15.73 % | 9.54 | 8.7649 |

Scoped capture (XLA default set minus CUSTOM_CALL) is safe with TE EP — settling the NCCLEP-006 "scope the command buffers" item — but is worth +0.03 pp; the overlap flag is ~−0.05 pp on both te_moe and a2a; `max_num_sms` is monotonically negative (auto > 32 > 16 — third falsification of SM budgeting on this stack after B200MFU-016/-021). The tuned seam reproduces its untuned 17.15 %. **The a2a_cute lead stands at ~1.3 pp over the best TE arm through every knob.** With quantization explicitly out of scope (fp8/MXFP8 wire not yet in `moe.py`), the remaining untested NVIDIA levers are the quantized block and the NGC stack.

NGC 26.06 status: the guarded-overlay machinery from #7421 works end-to-end for the bench (pinned wheel + per-sha JIT headers + patched PJRT plugin; 16×4 gang up, all ranks compiling), but the a2a_cute arm's `jit_train_step` compile under the NGC XLA has produced no output for >90 min (`/mwittmann/ngc-gc-a2a3`) — timeboxed and deferred along with the te_moe and ragged-dot-fusion-native NGC arms; will follow up.

Reproduction: branch `mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep-ncclep` @ 8664bb3c5 (`run_arms_gapclose{,2,3}.sh`, `launch_ngc.py`); tip-regression repro matrix in the [logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/research/mcwitt/7331-nccl-ep/.agents/logbooks/7331-nccl-ep.md) (NCCLEP-010). Ranked next: (1) report the tip regression + repro to NVIDIA (blocks #3231 validation); (2) quantized wire when `moe.py` grows it (#7282); (3) NGC arms once the compile stall is understood.

topics.title: [grug] Early hero checkpoints store router bias equal to their pending QB update
topics.body:
Checkpoints from the original hero run `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` store a router bias that already equals the bias derived from their own `pending_qb_betas`. A consistent step-N checkpoint cannot do that, so these checkpoints may mix state from two training steps.

The hero train step (`_make_train_step` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py`, same order at 12d8b6f0) overwrites the router bias with centered(−`pending_qb_betas`), runs the forward, backward, and optimizer update, then stores the step's new quantile-balancing betas as `pending_qb_betas`. The router bias has no gradient (`stop_gradient`), no weight decay, and all-zero Adam moments, so a step-N checkpoint should hold bias = centered(−β_{N−1}) and pending = β_N. Each β is a fresh per-step quantile estimate, so the two should differ.

Every checkpoint from step 114000 onward behaves as expected. On 9 permanent checkpoints from step 114000 to 264000, mean |stored bias − centered(−pending)| is 0.017–0.034 and the max is 1–7 logit units.

The six `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` checkpoints do not. At steps 6000, 12000, 24000, 36000, 48000, and 54000 under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-12d8b6f0-dee637/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/`, `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` equals centered(−`pending_qb_betas`) to at most 4.8e-7, which is fp32 rounding. The bf16 `params` bias equals bf16 of the master bias. That would require β_N = β_{N−1} + a per-layer constant at every save. This run used fp32 pinned-host master params (`MasterParamMode.FP32_PINNED_HOST`). The later runs keep fp32 `params` and no master.

Two explanations fit: the saved weights come from one step later than the saved `pending_qb_betas`, or the saved `pending_qb_betas` is one step stale. In both cases the checkpoint would combine two steps' state, possibly through the async save path and the donated train-state buffers in pinned-host master mode. None of this is verified.

Reproduce: read `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` and `pending_qb_betas` from one of the checkpoints above with tensorstore (`{"driver": "zarr3", "kvstore": {"driver": "ocdbt", "base": build_kvstore_spec(ckpt), "path": key + "/"}}`). Compare `bias` with `b - b.mean(-1, keepdims=True)` where `b = -pending`. Both arrays are [48, 384] float32.

Done when the cause is identified, and if it is a save-path bug, the affected checkpoint modes and steps are listed and the current save path is shown to be unaffected or fixed.

topics.title: [verifyit] Bound the judge call by the caller's deadline
topics.body:
A host judge call cannot stop at the verifier deadline of a rollout. RolloutEngine grades a judge task with `asyncio.to_thread(grade_remote_judge_answer, ...)` in `_grade_rollout` ([rolloutengine/grading.py:76](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L76), from #10203), and `grade_remote_judge_answer` calls the synchronous `grade_judge_candidate` ([taskcompendium/grading.py:179](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L179)). When the verifier deadline expires, the engine stops its wait, but the thread keeps waiting for the HTTP call. Each judge request has `JudgeSpec.request_timeout`, 120 s by default ([grade_judge.py:374](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L374), [:387](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L387), [:567](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L567)). For every rubric except labels, the OpenAI client retries a failed request up to two times ([grade_judge.py:462](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L462)). Thus one timed-out judge call can hold a thread for about 6 minutes.

The thread comes from the default executor of the event loop, which in-process grading (`grade_answer`, [rolloutengine/grading.py:78](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L78)) also uses. Its size is `min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4)`, 12 threads on an 8-CPU host. When a slow or unavailable judge holds all threads, an in-process grade of another attempt waits for a thread, and the wait counts against that attempt's verifier deadline. In a test with a 4-thread pool, 4 calls that blocked for 2 s and timed out after 0.1 s made the next call wait 1.6 s.

Done when:
- verifyit has a judge call that a caller can bound by a deadline: a timeout argument that sets the request timeout and the retries of the OpenAI client, or an async call that the caller can cancel.
- `grade_remote_judge_answer` passes the deadline through, and RolloutEngine gives it the remaining verifier time.
- A test shows that a judge call to a server that does not answer ends at the verifier deadline.

Found in the review of #10203 ([comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203#issuecomment-6240035622)).

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

On current main, `grade_judge_candidate` uses `JudgeSpec.request_timeout` for each synchronous HTTP request; the OpenAI client's automatic retries remain enabled for reference and checklist rubrics. `grade_remote_judge_answer` has no deadline parameter, and #10203's host-judge path runs it in the event loop's default executor under `asyncio.timeout`, which stops the wait but leaves the worker running. The same executor handles in-process grading, so stalled judge requests can delay unrelated attempts after their verifier deadlines expire.

**Relevant code**
- [`grade_judge.py#L213-L263`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L213-L263) — synchronous judge entry point
- [`grade_judge.py#L451-L473`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L451-L473) — client retry policy
- [`grading.py#L146-L184`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L146-L184) — missing deadline handoff
- [`grading.py#L56-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L56-L79) — host judge in the default executor
- [`engine.py#L210-L230`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L210-L230) — verifier wait deadline

# Proposed Fix

Follow-up to #10203, whose host-judge path is still under review:

1. Add an optional absolute monotonic deadline to `grade_judge_candidate`, pass it through `grade_remote_judge_answer`, report expiry as `GradingFailure.TIMEOUT`, and before every HTTP request (including label and manual score/budget retries) cap the timeout by `min(spec.request_timeout, remaining)` with OpenAI automatic retries disabled for deadline-bound calls.
2. Have RolloutEngine derive that deadline from its active verifier timeout after output capture and pass it into `asyncio.to_thread`, so time queued for an executor worker also consumes the budget.
3. Use a local HTTP server that accepts a request without answering to verify the judge worker releases a single executor slot near `verifier_timeout`, sends no retry, and lets an in-process grade proceed; cover label and reference/checklist requests and run the affected package suites and pre-commit checks.

A server that continually drips response bytes may still need a cancellable async judge path for a strict wall-clock bound.

topics.title: [post-training] Explore computer-use agents with text and code interfaces
topics.body:
TL;DR

Marin has not trained or evaluated any model on computer use: operating desktop, mobile or browser applications. Two Alibaba papers from this week release pieces a text-only model could use. This issue proposes RL on MAI-Gym's 42 synthetic apps through their text observation mode, and a computer-use baseline on OSWorld-v2 with OpenGCUA's code-first harness. Pixel-based tasks wait for vision support. No experiments have run yet.

Marin's agent post-training covers function calling, terminal and SWE tasks. Nothing covers graphical applications:

- No computer-use benchmark (OSWorld, AndroidWorld, WebArena) appears in the current eval policy ([#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197)). The nearest evals are the terminal benchmarks Terminal-Bench 2.1 and OT-TBLite.
- The harnesses we train and evaluate with (Terminus-2, Pi, mini-swe-agent, OpenCode) expose shell, file and function-call tools only. On these tasks, the Antidoom step-12 checkpoint of Snowball, Marin's post-trained 67B-A2B MoE, scores 31.1% on SWE-bench Verified and 10.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 ([#10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040#issuecomment-6158094013)).
- [#7418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7418) listed the web and OS agent sources from OpenThoughts-Agent (Mind2Web, go-browse, Synatra, nnetnav-live, AgentTuning WebShop/ALFWorld/OS). It left them unconverted because they need an interactive runtime to verify. All are text-only. The issue closed on October 6 in favour of sourcing our own RL data.
- Our models cannot read screenshots. Rui Li's SigLIP2 + Qwen3 baseline ([#2383](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2383)) did not merge. bkolligs is connecting SigLIP to Delphi 998M ([#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524), [PR #10076](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10076), open) and has no benchmark numbers yet.
- Shellbox machines return text and bytes only ([`machine.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L211-L248)). The QEMU backend is a headless microVM, and nobody has measured whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our nodes ([#9433](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9433)).
- Our largest sandbox run reached about 2,150 live gVisor sandboxes before the controller of Iris, our cluster scheduler, saturated ([#10111](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10111)). Work to move execution off the controller is open ([#10119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10119)).

TaskForge ([#10152](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10152)), our RL task generator, validates each task by replaying reference solutions and running agents that look for shortcuts. Its tasks so far are math and science problems in shells.

MAI-Gym

[MAI-Gym](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939) (Tong et al., 2026) runs GUI agents for evaluation and online RL through one rollout pipeline:

- Environments: Android in ReDroid containers, which avoids the nested virtualization the standard emulator needs; desktop VMs inside containers; headless Chromium for web. It reaches 20,000 parallel instances with warm pools and screenshots passed through object storage.
- Actions: coordinate clicks, typing and hotkeys, plus `bash` on desktops. Observations are screenshots, plus shell output on desktops.
- Synthetic apps: coding agents build resettable mock apps and cross-app scenarios. A verifier must score 0 on the initial state, 1 after a reference solution and 0 after reset.
- Training: Qwen3.5-9B (a vision-language model), SFT then GRPO. MAI-Gym-9B scores 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified (desktop) and 78.4% on MobileWorld (Android).
- Transfer: RL in a mock of the 12306 train-ticketing app raised success on 52 tasks in the real app, on a physical phone, from 28.8% to 48.1%.

Only part of it is released. The repository has the agent harness and 42 synthetic apps with 840 tasks. The framework, the synthesis skills and the 2,000 OSWorld/MobileWorld tasks are announced but not yet published.

Each released app is one HTML file with a deterministic state machine. Its manifest declares a text observation (`engine.a11y(state)`) and actions by element ID (`tap {id}`, `type {id, text}`). Verifiers are JSON checks on the app's final state. A text-only model can therefore run these tasks in a headless browser, with no screenshots.

OpenGCUA

[OpenGCUA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) (Zhou et al., 2026) studies harness design for computer use with existing frontier models. It releases no trained model.

- At each step the model writes one Python program. The program may call `pyautogui`, `bash()` and `subprocess`, and the prompt prefers `bash()` to GUI actions.
- The paper moves two decisions from fixed harness rules to the model: when to take a screenshot, and how to track task state, which the model does with a todo list.
- On the 82 OSWorld-v2 tasks that need no internet access, the mean partial score of eight models rose from 45.3 with GUI-only batched actions to 64.9 with this code-first harness. Steps per task fell 53%. The weakest GUI-only models gained the most: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rose from 28.0 to 57.7.

The paper runs no text-only configuration, so we analysed its released trajectories. Models requested a screenshot in 26–60% of steps. Each model used no GUI actions on 4 to 18 tasks, and only 5 of the 82 tasks were solved by some model with neither GUI actions nor screenshots. A text-only model would solve few of these tasks, but the shell-first design matches what our models already do well.

Licences

- MAI-Gym's repository has no licence file, so the apps and tasks need the authors' permission before we train on them.
- OpenGCUA's code is Apache-2.0. Its trajectories carry no licence, and most are outputs of closed models.
- OSWorld-v2 is Apache-2.0.

Goal: give Marin a computer-use evaluation and a first training signal for graphical applications, starting with interfaces a text-only model can use.

Hypotheses:

1. RL on a training split of MAI-Gym's synthetic apps, using text observations, raises Snowball's success on held-out apps. Function calling (BFCL-Parity), Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified do not regress.
2. With OpenGCUA's code-first harness and no screenshots, Snowball solves some of the 82 offline OSWorld-v2 tasks. That score is the text-only baseline a vision-capable model must beat.

Proposed steps:

1. Ask the MAI-Gym authors about licensing the apps and tasks.
2. Run the 42 apps in a headless browser behind a Shellbox backend that exposes the text observation and ID actions, with the existing verifiers as rewards. Hold out whole apps for evaluation, and check the tasks with TaskForge's validation. The same backend could later host the web sources from #7418.
3. Measure the Snowball baseline on the held-out apps, then run RL with Marin's rollout engine ([#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623)).
4. Check whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our Iris nodes. If it is, run OSWorld-v2 with the OpenGCUA harness in a desktop VM. Without KVM, the QEMU backend falls back to software emulation (TCG), which is slower.
5. Revisit pixel-based tasks when [#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524) produces a vision model at a useful scale.

Proposed. No owner yet. Computer use is not on any current roadmap.

Links

* Papers: [MAI-Gym, arXiv 2610.20939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939); [OpenGCUA, arXiv 2610.22200](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200)
* MAI-Gym code and apps: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym) (apps in `site/apps/`); model: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B](https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B)
* OpenGCUA code: [Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA) (OSWorld agents in `packages/harness/examples/osworld/`); trajectories: [viewer](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html)
* Benchmark: [xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2)
* Android containers: [ReDroid](https://github.com/remote-android/redroid-doc)
* Related: [#10189](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10189) (web-search agents)

```markdown
- The harnesses we train and evaluate with (Terminus-2, Pi, mini-swe-agent, OpenCode) expose shell, file and function-call tools only. On these tasks, the Antidoom step-12 checkpoint of Snowball, Marin's post-trained 67B-A2B MoE, scores 31.1% on SWE-bench Verified and 10.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 ([#10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040#issuecomment-6158094013)).
- [#7418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7418) listed the web and OS agent sources from OpenThoughts-Agent (Mind2Web, go-browse, Synatra, nnetnav-live, AgentTuning WebShop/ALFWorld/OS). It left them unconverted because they need an interactive runtime to verify. All are text-only. The issue closed on October 6 in favour of sourcing our own RL data.
- Our models cannot read screenshots. Rui Li's SigLIP2 + Qwen3 baseline ([#2383](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2383)) did not merge. bkolligs is connecting SigLIP to Delphi 998M ([#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524), [PR #10076](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10076), open) and has no benchmark numbers yet.
- Shellbox machines return text and bytes only ([`machine.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L211-L248)). The QEMU backend is a headless microVM, and nobody has measured whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our nodes ([#9433](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9433)).
- Our largest sandbox run reached about 2,150 live gVisor sandboxes before the controller of Iris, our cluster scheduler, saturated ([#10111](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10111)). Work to move execution off the controller is open ([#10119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10119)).

TaskForge ([#10152](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10152)), our RL task generator, validates each task by replaying reference solutions and running agents that look for shortcuts. Its tasks so far are math and science problems in shells.

### MAI-Gym

[MAI-Gym](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939) (Tong et al., 2026) runs GUI agents for evaluation and online RL through one rollout pipeline:

- Environments: Android in ReDroid containers, which avoids the nested virtualization the standard emulator needs; desktop VMs inside containers; headless Chromium for web. It reaches 20,000 parallel instances with warm pools and screenshots passed through object storage.
- Actions: coordinate clicks, typing and hotkeys, plus `bash` on desktops. Observations are screenshots, plus shell output on desktops.
- Synthetic apps: coding agents build resettable mock apps and cross-app scenarios. A verifier must score 0 on the initial state, 1 after a reference solution and 0 after reset.
- Training: Qwen3.5-9B (a vision-language model), SFT then GRPO. MAI-Gym-9B scores 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified (desktop) and 78.4% on MobileWorld (Android).
- Transfer: RL in a mock of the 12306 train-ticketing app raised success on 52 tasks in the real app, on a physical phone, from 28.8% to 48.1%.

Only part of it is released. The repository has the agent harness and 42 synthetic apps with 840 tasks. The framework, the synthesis skills and the 2,000 OSWorld/MobileWorld tasks are announced but not yet published.

Each released app is one HTML file with a deterministic state machine. Its manifest declares a text observation (`engine.a11y(state)`) and actions by element ID (`tap {id}`, `type {id, text}`). Verifiers are JSON checks on the app's final state. A text-only model can therefore run these tasks in a headless browser, with no screenshots.

### OpenGCUA

[OpenGCUA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) (Zhou et al., 2026) studies harness design for computer use with existing frontier models. It releases no trained model.

- At each step the model writes one Python program. The program may call `pyautogui`, `bash()` and `subprocess`, and the prompt prefers `bash()` to GUI actions.
- The paper moves two decisions from fixed harness rules to the model: when to take a screenshot, and how to track task state, which the model does with a todo list.
- On the 82 OSWorld-v2 tasks that need no internet access, the mean partial score of eight models rose from 45.3 with GUI-only batched actions to 64.9 with this code-first harness. Steps per task fell 53%. The weakest GUI-only models gained the most: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rose from 28.0 to 57.7.

The paper runs no text-only configuration, so we analysed its released trajectories. Models requested a screenshot in 26–60% of steps. Each model used no GUI actions on 4 to 18 tasks, and only 5 of the 82 tasks were solved by some model with neither GUI actions nor screenshots. A text-only model would solve few of these tasks, but the shell-first design matches what our models already do well.

### Licences

- MAI-Gym's repository has no licence file, so the apps and tasks need the authors' permission before we train on them.
- OpenGCUA's code is Apache-2.0. Its trajectories carry no licence, and most are outputs of closed models.
- OSWorld-v2 is Apache-2.0.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Goal: give Marin a computer-use evaluation and a first training signal for graphical applications, starting with interfaces a text-only model can use.

Hypotheses:

1. RL on a training split of MAI-Gym's synthetic apps, using text observations, raises Snowball's success on held-out apps. Function calling (BFCL-Parity), Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified do not regress.
2. With OpenGCUA's code-first harness and no screenshots, Snowball solves some of the 82 offline OSWorld-v2 tasks. That score is the text-only baseline a vision-capable model must beat.

Proposed steps:

1. Ask the MAI-Gym authors about licensing the apps and tasks.
2. Run the 42 apps in a headless browser behind a Shellbox backend that exposes the text observation and ID actions, with the existing verifiers as rewards. Hold out whole apps for evaluation, and check the tasks with TaskForge's validation. The same backend could later host the web sources from #7418.
3. Measure the Snowball baseline on the held-out apps, then run RL with Marin's rollout engine ([#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623)).
4. Check whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our Iris nodes. If it is, run OSWorld-v2 with the OpenGCUA harness in a desktop VM. Without KVM, the QEMU backend falls back to software emulation (TCG), which is slower.
5. Revisit pixel-based tasks when [#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524) produces a vision model at a useful scale.

## Status

Proposed. No owner yet. Computer use is not on any current roadmap.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:
* Papers: [MAI-Gym, arXiv 2610.20939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939); [OpenGCUA, arXiv 2610.22200](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200)
* MAI-Gym code and apps: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym) (apps in `site/apps/`); model: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B](https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B)
* OpenGCUA code: [Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA) (OSWorld agents in `packages/harness/examples/osworld/`); trajectories: [viewer](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html)
* Benchmark: [xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2)
* Android containers: [ReDroid](https://github.com/remote-android/redroid-doc)
* Related: [#10189](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10189) (web-search agents)

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

```

</details>

🤖
# Research

MAI-Gym currently publishes 42 app directories with text observations and ID actions, but its repository has no license and its framework source is still promised for a later release ([repository](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym), [example manifest](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym/blob/main/site/apps/anvil_remit/manifest.json)). Marin's merged rollout engine uses Shellbox task sessions; [#10203](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203) is replacing those sessions with registered harnesses, and [#9787](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9787) already implements TaskForge validation trials. OSWorld needs a separate VM evaluation path, and its [v2.1 release](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2#benchmark-versions) requires matching code, tasks, assets, and websites. No open PR found for MAI-Gym or OSWorld integration.

**Relevant code**
- [`machine.py#L211-L248`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L211-L248) — Shellbox execution contract.
- [`task_session.py#L117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/task_session.py#L117) — current task interaction loop.
- [`spec.py#L52`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/spec.py#L52) — task runtime selection.

# Proposed Fix

1. Resolve MAI-Gym app/task training and redistribution permission and pin an upstream revision. Until then, prototype with a Marin-authored toy app; keep MAI-Gym assets out of training and published artifacts. Record the permission and exact app/task inventory in this issue.
2. After #10203 lands, add a browser harness for one app: deterministic reset, `a11y` observation, element-ID `tap`/`type`, step and time limits, and private final-state grading. Reuse #9787's solver, adversary, and control checks; admit a task only when initial/reference/reset scores are 0/1/0 and invalid actions fail safely.
3. With permission and validated tasks, pin an app-level train/held-out split before training. Run a Snowball text-only baseline on held-out apps, publishing per-app and aggregate success, trial counts, failures, and replay traces. Then train with the existing rollout engine and compare the same held-out split, plus BFCL-Parity, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and SWE-bench Verified. Coordinate any canonical benchmark claim with [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197).
4. Treat OSWorld as a separate pilot: pin the `osworld-v2.1` release and matching assets, audit which of the 82 offline tasks have useful text/code paths, check `/dev/kvm` on an Iris worker without changing cluster state, then run a small OpenGCUA code-harness baseline. Publish task-level scores, screenshots used, latency, and infrastructure failures before scaling; track controller capacity under [#10119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10119).

The licensing decision gates MAI-Gym training; #10203 gates the browser harness interface. The OSWorld pilot can proceed independently after the task audit and KVM check.

topics.title: Build RL launches with the pinned recipe package
topics.body:
Build RL launches from typed immutable recipe parts before submitting jobs. The Marin adapter contributes the fixed Megatron and local-engine policy; producers author their training settings and resource counts, and the native launcher derives the role allocation and runtime profile.

`marin-core` depends on the recipe package through a Git subdirectory at the launcher commit. The external updater advances the requirement and locks together; recipe-package-only lock changes select the launch-document compatibility test. Users of PyPI `marin-core` who import `marin.rl.skyrl` must install `marinskyrl-recipe` separately at the launcher commit.

Current producer documents load and persist through the locked launcher. Complete comparisons preserve baseline-loadable documents apart from the launcher pin, with the reviewed bundled-recipe path and ordering differences. Lint, types, package and updater checks pass.

The full Levanter TPU selection, triggered by the lock change, exceeds the 25-minute job limit on main as well ([main run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/37368535084)).

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#933.
