topics.title: [drafting] DSpark drafters for Snowball (Grug-67B-A2B): itw vs targetgen training, serving, and RL status
topics.body:
Related: #9079 (EAGLE-3 PoC), #9114 (adapted EAGLE-3 draft), #9312 (drafting tracker), #9735 (Snowball broad-domain RLVR).

## 1. Overview

We trained two DSpark drafters for [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) and measured them in vLLM against plain decoding. Both have the same architecture and recipe (3 decoder layers, hidden 2560, FFN 3840, block size 8, 32k draft vocabulary, 280M parameters). They differ in the text they train on, which we call *itw* and *targetgen*:

| | itw drafter | targetgen drafter |
|---|---|---|
| Training text | the gold replies of the Datakit SFT mix (the data the target was fine-tuned on) | the target's own replies (T=1) to 270k sampled Datakit conversations |
| Training length | 80,813 steps, about 9.7B tokens, 21% of one epoch (stopped at a time limit; learning rate not yet decayed) | 17,737 steps, 2.1B tokens, one epoch (learning rate decayed to zero) |
| Compute (2 GB200 nodes) | about 11.7 h of training | 10.2 h of generation + 3.0 h of merge and training |

**Naming.** *itw* (in-the-wild) means the drafter trains on text that already exists, here the replies in the Datakit SFT mix (earlier notes and run names call this "offline" or "off-policy"). *targetgen* (target-generated) means it trains on the target model's own regenerated replies (earlier: "on-policy" or "online").

Main findings:

- Both drafters speed up Snowball decoding: about 1.8x to 2.2x output tokens/s over plain decoding at concurrency 16 (1.5x on later-turn Datakit prompts), with acceptance lengths of 2.8 to 3.1 (2.4 to 2.6 on later turns) (Section 3.1).
- The itw drafter is ahead of the targetgen drafter on every set we measured, by about 0.3 in acceptance length. One epoch of targetgen data did not make up for having 4.6 times fewer training tokens.
- Both drafters transfer to the Dr. Doom fine-tune of the target (acceptance falls by 0.4 to 0.5; the speed-up over plain decoding stays at 1.6x to 1.8x) (Section 3.1).
- The drafter loads in the pinned Marin vLLM fork unchanged. It needs `draft_sample_method: probabilistic` and `rejection_sample_method: standard` set in the serving config for sampled decoding; these are not stored in the checkpoint (Section 4).
- The trainer's validation `accept_len` overstates serving acceptance by about 0.6 to 0.9 tokens, mainly because serving chains its rounds (Section 3.2).
- For RL: the split layout (policy and engines on separate nodes) ran one full RL step with the drafter intact. `colocate_all` does not work with a draft today (acceptance falls to 1.0). The MarinSkyRL change that accepts `dspark` in the managed config is on a [fork branch](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding) and has not yet been run for several steps (Section 3.4).

## 2. Methodology

### 2.1 Target and drafter

- Target: [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) (`grug_moe`, hidden 2560, 26 layers, 256 experts), served by vLLM's [`grugmoe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py).
- Drafter: DSpark (DFlash plus a Markov logit-bias head and a confidence head), added to vLLM in [vllm-project/vllm#46995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46995); the draft model class is [`qwen3_dspark.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py). The architecture is set by [`draft_config.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/draft_config.json) and the training recipe by [`settings.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/settings.sh):
  - 3 `qwen3`-type layers, FFN 3840 (1.5 x hidden), 20 heads / 5 KV heads, block size 8;
  - hidden states tapped from target layers 2, 12, 22 plus the final layer;
  - 32,000-token draft vocabulary built from the supervised-token frequencies of the training text; the drafter's `lm_head` equals the target's `lm_head` rows for those tokens, bit for bit (checked on both drafters);
  - Markov head rank 256 (vanilla), confidence head; loss 0.1 CE + 0.9 TV against the target's distribution; learning rate 3e-4; 12,288 anchors per 32,768-token sequence.
- Training code: our fork of vllm-project/speculators, branch [`grug-dspark-gate`](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/tree/grug-dspark-gate), with three changes on top of upstream: Grug's gated final norm in the DFlash/DSpark targets and `grug_moe` registration ([f93d1a5](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/f93d1a57998f552a716322925c19eae8d9202342)), `launch_vllm.py` reading the layer count from `config.json` ([96699f9](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/96699f9ad8740040ed18cf2a9443ec33dd740dad)), and HF-style step checkpoints ([99a50bf](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/99a50bf3977776a4a0f5548e5a25e28e6cdd396a)). Not upstream.

### 2.2 Data: the Datakit SFT mix

The training prompts are the data the target was fine-tuned on: the 203-source Datakit SFT mixture. It was downloaded and processed with [`build_datakit_sft_mix.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/build_datakit_sft_mix.py) (`fetch`, `stats`, `select`, `write`) through [`fetch.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/fetch.sbatch) / [`submit_fetch.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/submit_fetch.sh) and [`write.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/write.sbatch), following the per-source token allocations in Marin's [`special_token_1000_mix.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82620ad62bbe23b9b12a89d656c24e6f80aff91a/experiments/grug_sft/special_token_1000_mix.json) (commit `82620ad`; the same allocations are on the model repo as [`training_data_mix.json`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21/blob/main/training_data_mix.json)).

1. Plan. [`plan_datakit_sft_mix.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/plan_datakit_sft_mix.py) resolves each source to a Hugging Face repo and pinned revision (output [`plan.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/plan.json); about 628 GB across 160 unique downloads; locations of the normalized outputs in [`normalized_paths.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/normalized_paths.json)).
2. Fetch and select. Marin's per-source download and normalize steps run through `build_datakit_sft_mix.py fetch`, then `stats` and `select` allocate tokens per source.
3. Write. Render with the Grug chat template, tokenize, clip rows at 32,768 tokens, and write an Arrow dataset of `input_ids` and an assistant-token `loss_mask`; [`finalize_dataset.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/finalize_dataset.py) checks it and writes the token-frequency file.

Result: 6,471,159 rows in 215 shards, 45.99B tokens after the clip (53.4B before; 313,449 rows were clipped), of which 24.33B tokens are supervised assistant tokens; per-source counts are in the dataset's `manifest.json` ([`training_data_manifest.json`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016/blob/main/training_data_manifest.json), also in the targetgen repo). The last 0.1% of rows is held out for validation. The dataset itself is not published; it is rebuilt by the scripts above. Decisions and the Marin commit choice are in [`PLAN.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/PLAN.md).

### 2.3 Training setup (both experiments)

Hidden states are extracted online, as in the [Qwen3-0.6B runs](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_qwen3_0_6b_nemotron-terminal-corpus_itw/NOTES.md): a vLLM server runs the target and hands hidden states to the trainer through [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake), so nothing is stored on disk. On each of 2 Vista GB200 nodes, 2 GPUs serve the target (TP=1, DP2 x EP2) next to their own `mooncake_master`, and 2 GPUs train; the 4 trainer ranks run as one DDP job. A step is about 120,000 tokens and takes 0.52 s. The entry points are [`vista/run_2node_ddp.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/run_2node_ddp.sh), [`vista/run_2node_ddp.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/run_2node_ddp.sbatch) and [`vista/submit_chain.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/submit_chain.sh) (a chain of resumable 12 h jobs). Metrics go to W&B project [`atutej/marin_speculator`](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator).

### 2.4 Experiment A: itw drafter

Train on the dataset as written: the gold Datakit replies stand in for the target's completions. One epoch would be 382,747 steps (45.95B tokens); the run was stopped by the time limit at step 80,813 (about 9.7B tokens), so the learning rate (linear decay over the full epoch) had not annealed. The checkpoint we evaluate is `checkpoint-80813`. W&B runs for the three resumed segments: [jgsst5k0](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/jgsst5k0), [71rm9vy8](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/71rm9vy8), [ij7oistz](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/ij7oistz). The trainer's validation `accept_len` at step 80,813 (3.785) is recorded in [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md).

### 2.5 Experiment B: targetgen drafter

Same dataset, drafter and recipe, but the supervised text is the target's own. The experiment folder is [`dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen). It is a chain of two 2-node jobs submitted by `vista/submit_chain.sh`:

1. **Regenerate** (`vista/run_regen.sh` with [`regenerate_token_rows.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/regenerate_token_rows.py)). 270,000 rows (4.2% of the train split) are sampled uniformly without replacement. Each node runs its own vLLM (DP4 x EP4, 512 concurrent sequences) on half the rows. For each assistant turn in order, the prompt is everything before it (the original non-assistant tokens plus the target's own earlier turns), the target generates the turn at T=1, top_p=1, up to 32,768 new tokens, stopping at `<|eot_id|>`; the generated tokens (mask 1) replace the original turn, and the original tokens that follow it (tool output, next user turn) are kept with mask 0. A row is cut at 32,768 tokens in total.
2. **Merge and train.** The parts are merged into an Arrow dataset (shuffled), the 32k draft vocabulary is rebuilt from the target's own regenerated tokens (it covers 98.06% of them), and the same 2-node training runs one epoch. The itw run's `run_2node_ddp.sh` is reused with this experiment's settings. The merged dataset has 2.13B tokens. W&B run: [6wnqmuwi](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/6wnqmuwi). The final validation metrics (`accept_len` 3.724) are in [`targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json).

Regeneration statistics, from the final lines of the two regeneration logs ([`targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt)): 1.229B generated tokens (about 4,550 per row), 0 errors, 5.0% of rows ended on the 32k per-turn cap, 0.4% ran into the window limit; generation ran at 16.7k to 19.2k tokens/s per node, averaged over the run. In a 3,000-row pilot, 26% of rows were multi-turn (7.4 regenerated turns on average).

We used our own token-level regenerator, not the speculators `regenerate-responses` CLI, because the dataset stores token ids with a loss mask and no chat messages. Going through the CLI means decoding each row back to messages and tools ([`rows_to_messages.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/rows_to_messages.py); the round trip is exact on 98.4% of 500 sampled rows) and then training on one row per generation with the whole prefix repeated: 3.8 times more training tokens on a 3,000-row sample, 10.6 times for multi-turn rows ([`boundary_layout_inflation.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/boundary_layout_inflation.py); output and the round-trip check in [`regenerate_responses_cli_cost.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/regenerate_responses_cli_cost.txt)).

### 2.6 Evaluation

Every arm serves the target in the pinned Marin vLLM fork, [`marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c), the same wheel [MarinSkyRL pins](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/pyproject.toml#L100). Settings are `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` on one GB200 node, one server at a time on an otherwise idle node, concurrency 16, T=1, top_p=1. The drafter arms use `{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 8, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "standard"}`; plain decoding is the baseline. Concurrency 16 matches the `max_num_seqs: 16` per engine in the RL config ([`glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/configs/glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml)).

- Acceptance length is `1 + accepted/drafts` from vLLM's speculative-decoding counters, using the definition in speculators' [`perf_utils.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/blob/main/scripts/evaluate/perf_utils.py), over the whole chained rollout.
- Throughput is generated tokens divided by wall time for the whole set; the gain is the ratio to the plain-decoding arm on the same prompts.
- Harness: [`serve_eval.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/serve_eval.sh) (one server per arm) and [`run_eval.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/run_eval.py) (prompts, sampling, counters); for batch jobs, [`eval_arms.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/eval_arms.sbatch) and [`submit_eval.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/submit_eval.sh).

Prompt sets (manifests with seeds and hashes: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/prompt_manifests/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/prompt_manifests)):

- **(a) RL prompts.** Rows of the Snowball broad-domain RLVR training set, [`open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) (the corrected preparation described in the campaign's [`CLEANED_DATASET.md`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/audits/CLEANED_DATASET.md); train split), rendered as the RL requests carry them: stored messages (including earlier assistant tool calls and tool outputs), each row's tool schemas (the `request_json` column) passed as `tools=`, and the chat template's default `Reasoning: /think` (the [RL config](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/configs/glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml) passes no `chat_template_kwargs`; the [template](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) defaults to `/think`). Generation settings follow the same config: up to 49,152 new tokens per turn, 102,400-token window, T=1. 1,024 prompts sampled at random; we ran the first 256, which are themselves a uniform sample. Mix of the 1,024: tool use 389, instruction following 148, code 94, math 55, MCQA 44, MultiChallenge 41, others; 229 prompts already contain tool-call history. Built by [`build_nemotron_rlvr_prompts.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/build_nemotron_rlvr_prompts.py).
- **(b) Datakit validation prompts, multi-turn.** 1,024 prompts from the 6,472 held-out Datakit rows, which neither drafter trained on. For each row a uniformly random assistant turn is chosen, with the dataset's earlier turns as context: 833 first-turn and 191 later-turn prompts (median context 3,119 tokens, longest 27,450). Replies capped at 4,096 tokens. Built by [`build_val_prompts.py --turns random`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/build_val_prompts.py).
- **(c) Dr. Doom target.** The same RL-prompt run with the target replaced by [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom) (the FTPO de-looping fine-tune). Both drafters were trained against the 09.21 hidden states, so this measures transfer to a fine-tuned target.

### 2.7 RL integration

MarinSkyRL (pin [`5de48d34`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/5de48d34), vLLM wheel as above) was run on Vista GB200 with the DSpark drafter in an R2E-Gym RL setup. The infrastructure notes are in [`docs/rl_dspark_infra.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/rl_dspark_infra.md) and the A/B notes in [`r2egym-rl-ab/NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_r2egym-rl-ab/NOTES.md). The two layouts are [`2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml) (split, `weight_sync_transport: expert_block`) and [`…_rl_coloc.yaml`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl_coloc.yaml) (`colocate_all`). The managed [`generator.speculative_decoding`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/marinskyrl/speculative_decoding.py#L26-L29) block accepts only `eagle3`. A branch on a fork, [`atutej/MarinSkyRL:dspark-speculative-decoding`](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding), adds three commits on top of Marin main: `dspark` as a method ([203c6f9d](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/203c6f9d909307e8f6ac288f9d320f349c43bb8b)), optional `draft_sample_method` / `rejection_sample_method` fields ([d2c23a89](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/d2c23a8921658aaf8a8d9211dbcc693d9a9490c8)), and the post-weight-sync refresh of the draft head for `dspark` ([9a0ea386](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/9a0ea386eaf6ccc35391ebe3fba2d5744a3f2cb6)).

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Acceptance length and throughput

**(a) RL prompts**, 09.21 target, first 256 prompts, replies up to 49,152 tokens (mean about 11k tokens, 11.7% hit the cap). Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-09.21/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-09.21).

| Arm | Acceptance length | Output tokens/s | Gain vs plain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain decoding | n/a | 1,960 | 1.00x |
| itw drafter, step 80,813 | **3.141** | 4,226 | **2.16x** |
| targetgen drafter, step 17,737 | 2.835 | 3,696 | 1.89x |

**(a2) RL prompts on the Dr. Doom target** ([`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom)), same 256 prompts and settings (replies up to 49,152 tokens; mean about 16k tokens, 20.7% hit the cap). Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-dr-doom/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-dr-doom).

| Arm | Acceptance length | Output tokens/s | Gain vs plain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain decoding | n/a | 2,023 | 1.00x |
| itw drafter, step 80,813 | **2.667** | 3,630 | **1.79x** |
| targetgen drafter, step 17,737 | 2.465 | 3,270 | 1.62x |

Both drafters were trained on the 09.21 target's hidden states, so this is transfer to a fine-tuned target. Acceptance falls by 0.47 (itw) and 0.37 (targetgen) relative to table (a), and the speed-up over plain decoding stays at 1.6x to 1.8x. The ordering of the two drafters is the same.

**(b) Datakit validation prompts, multi-turn**, 09.21 target, 1,024 prompts, replies up to 4,096 tokens. Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_multiturn_1024/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_multiturn_1024).

| Subset | Plain tok/s | itw: acceptance length | tok/s | gain | targetgen: acceptance length | tok/s | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First turn (833) | 2,131 | **3.188** | 4,401 | **2.07x** | 2.879 | 4,004 | 1.88x |
| Later turn (191) | 1,613 | **2.601** | 2,529 | **1.57x** | 2.373 | 2,339 | 1.45x |
| Pooled (1,024) | 2,066 | **3.122** | 4,113 | **1.99x** | 2.821 | 3,749 | 1.81x |

Supplementary, earlier runs with the same harness (raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/r2egym_1024_greedy/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/r2egym_1024_greedy)): on 1,024 R2E-Gym first-turn prompts with greedy drafting the two drafters are close (acceptance length 2.245 for the itw and 2.321 for the targetgen drafter; gains 1.51x and 1.54x). Later turns are harder than first turns for both drafters (Table b).

### 3.2 Trainer metric versus serving

The validation `accept_len` the trainer logs is 3.785 (itw, step 80,813, on Datakit validation rows; [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md)) and 3.724 (targetgen, final, on its own held-out rows; [`targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json)). Serving gives less, for two reasons we could separate:

- The trainer averages the accepted length of one draft round started at each of many positions, equally weighted. Serving chains rounds: after a long accepted run it skips an easy stretch, after a short one it stays in the hard spot, so its number is closer to a harmonic mean. Measured with the same text, a single round from uniformly random positions in the target's own replies gives 3.642 (itw) and 3.271 (targetgen) ([raw probe results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/random_anchor_probe_target_replies)), against 3.122 and 2.826 chained on the same Datakit validation prompts with probabilistic drafting ([raw results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_firstturn_1024_probabilistic)). On the targetgen run's own held-out rows (long multi-turn contexts, supervised anchors) the one-round numbers are 3.855 and 3.501 ([raw probe results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/random_anchor_probe_heldout_targetgen_rows)).
- Greedy drafting costs about 0.3 more than probabilistic drafting (for the itw drafter 2.660 against 2.973 on an earlier 128-prompt set; see [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md)).

Teacher-forced parity between the trainer's drafter and vLLM's drafter was checked: they pick the same token in 97 to 98% of slots, with equal acceptance on common anchors, so we found no implementation mismatch (also in `NOTES.md`). One residual remains unexplained: on its own held-out rows the targetgen drafter reaches 3.50 in the one-round probe against the trainer's 3.72. The probe is [`probe_random_anchor.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/probe_random_anchor.py) with the launcher [`probe_serve.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/probe_serve.sh).

### 3.3 Cost

| | itw | targetgen |
|---|---|---|
| Generation | none | 10.2 h on 2 nodes (1.23B tokens) |
| Merge and training | about 11.7 h of training for 80,813 steps | 3.0 h for 17,737 steps (includes about 0.5 h merge) |
| Training tokens | about 9.7B | 2.1B |

The targetgen budget was chosen to match the itw run's wall time (about 12 to 14 h on 2 nodes). The two runs are not matched in training tokens or in learning-rate schedule. Job records: Slurm accounting for the targetgen chain (regen 10:14:45, train 03:02:50) in [`targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt).

### 3.4 RL status

- **Split layout** (policy on one node, one DP4 x EP4 engine on another, [`weight_sync_transport: expert_block`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml), Triton MoE backend): one RL step ran end to end with the drafter intact (accept length 2.54 in the step-1 rollouts; the weight sync after training took 1.5 s). The default broadcast sync ran out of memory in this layout. The run failed later in a way we have not diagnosed, so we do not yet have acceptance after a weight sync. Details: [`docs/rl_dspark_infra.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/rl_dspark_infra.md).
- **`colocate_all`** ([config](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl_coloc.yaml)): the draft did not survive. Accept length was 1.000 in both runs. Engines sleep during training, and a [probe](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/tools/sleep_wake_probe.py) showed that sleep level 2 discards the draft's weights; our level-1 [patch](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/setup/machines/vista/patches/marinskyrl-sleep-level.patch) is not confirmed in an RL run. The managed `speculative_decoding` block rejects `colocate_all=true` at launch; our colocated runs passed `speculative_config` through the engine kwargs directly, which bypasses that check.
- **Draft head after weight sync:** MarinSkyRL re-slices the draft's `lm_head` from the updated policy after each sync, but only for [`eagle3`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/vllm/vllm_engine.py#L594), using vLLM's [`refresh_target_owned_draft_weights`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/v1/spec_decode/online_eagle.py#L89). The DSpark drafter's head is the same kind of frozen slice (bit-identical to the target's rows), so [the fork branch](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/9a0ea386eaf6ccc35391ebe3fba2d5744a3f2cb6) extends the refresh to `dspark`. The refresh has not been exercised in a multi-step RL run.
- The drafter is not trained during RL, so acceptance is expected to decay as the policy moves away from the 09.21 weights.

### 3.5 Limitations

- We have not run RL with these drafters yet; Section 3.4 is the state of that work.
- In MarinSkyRL, colocating the draft with the policy (`colocate_all`) currently disables it: acceptance falls to 1.0.

## 4. Artifacts and reproduction

- Drafters (`config.json`, `config.py`, `model.safetensors` each), uploaded with [`upload_drafter_to_hf.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/upload_drafter_to_hf.py): [`atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016) and [`atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen-20261016`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen-20261016)
- Serving recipe, tested with the pinned fork [`marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c):

  ```
  vllm serve open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "<drafter repo>", "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
                           "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "standard"}'
  ```
  The fork needs no changes: vLLM reads the checkpoint's `speculators_config` with its own [parser](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/base.py) and does not import the `speculators` package. The sampling fields are not stored in the checkpoint.
- Code: [`atutej/spec-experiments`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments) (branch `grug-full-run-and-rl`, commit `91e20d3`), [`atutej/speculators@grug-dspark-gate`](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/tree/grug-dspark-gate), [`atutej/MarinSkyRL@dspark-speculative-decoding`](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding).
- W&B: project [`atutej/marin_speculator`](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator).

topics.title: [grug] Honor dynamic attention bounds in reference backends
topics.body:
Honor the per-query bounds that the hero layer scan uses to select local attention windows in the reference and XLA attention backends. These backends previously ignored the bounds and silently evaluated local layers with full-causal attention.

Zero outputs for fully masked padding queries and reject precomputed bounds in Splash, which does not support them. Scan regressions compare outputs and Q/K/V gradients across local windows, packed segments, and padding. The XLA fallback materializes a dense mask; the active FA4 kernels are unchanged.

topics.title: Agent MoE Experiment: per-head MuonH on MLA kv-latent projections (d1024, d2048)
topics.body:
Try **per-head MuonH** on the MLA kv-latent up-projections: orthogonalize each head's `(kv_lora, head_dim)` block independently instead of the full `(kv_lora, n·head_dim)` matrix. Per `experiments/grug/moe/ablation_runbook.md`.

**Branch:** https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/grug/moe-abl/per-head-muon-kv

## Verbatim prompt

> lets follow ablation doc and make a new issue. lets try per head muon, where the projections from kv_latent -> k and v have muon applied seperately per head. this way, the projection from 512->1024 is replaced with 512->128. lets also run at d2048, where we replace 512->2048 with 512->128. only apply the change to the K and V projections. Leave Q as is. Apply in whichever way is simplest: custom reshape in optimizer, or storing parameters in stacked shape. This should be 2 runs, one for each size.

## Change under test

`w_uk` (kv_latent → k_nope) and `w_uv` (kv_latent → v) are `(kv_lora=512, n·head_dim)`. Muon currently Newton-Schulzes them as one matrix. This ablation orthogonalizes **each head's `(512, 128)` block separately** — so the `512→n·128` projection becomes `n` independent `512→128` orthogonalizations:
- **d1024**: n=8 → `512→1024` becomes 8× `512→128`.
- **d2048**: n=16 → `512→2048` becomes 16× `512→128`.

**Only K and V** (`w_uk`, `w_uv`). **Q (`w_uq`) is unchanged** (full-matrix Muon).

Implementation (simplest = **custom reshape in the optimizer**): `SCALE_MUON_PER_HEAD_KV=1` makes `grugmuon`'s `transform_array` split the trailing `n·128` axis of `w_uk`/`w_uv`, vmap the replicated NS over the (head, scan-layer) batch, and reshape back. No model/forward/sharding change, so scan stays on and the runs are directly comparable to the `mla-base` LR-sweep points. Verified: each head block is semi-orthogonal (col err ≈ 0.078, normal for 5-step quintic) and differs from full-matrix NS.

## Runs (2, MLA, ablation defaults, scan on)

Both: MLA `SCALE_MLA_HEAD_MULT=1`, qk 192, all-global (`SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW=4096`), datakit 2-phase, evals on, s3, MuonH base LR, `SCALE_MUON_PER_HEAD_KV=1`.

| run id | size | GPUs | layers | batch / steps | base LR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gb200-d1024-mla-perheadmuon-kv` | d1024 | 4 | 12 | 256 / 4768 | 0.015281 |
| `gb200-d2048-mla-perheadmuon-kv` | d2048 | 16 | 24 | 1024 / 11921 | 0.011093 |

Baselines: the `mla-base` points from the LR sweep (#7381) — same config with full-matrix Muon on w_uk/w_uv.

topics.title: [grug] Register symmetric buffers for hero all-gather and reduce-scatter
topics.body:
On the ragged all-to-all backend, the hero template registers NCCL symmetric buffers for the model's all-gather and reduce-scatter collectives in addition to the ragged transport. Levanter's `RAGGED_REQUIRED_XLA_FLAGS` keeps only the `raggedalltoall` registration that the device-initiated transport needs, so other users of that constant, such as the ragged EP test harness, are unchanged. The template keeps the flag non-overridable, like the transport flags.

Against #9333 alone, this change makes a typical update 0.24% faster, but it does not yet show a significant gain in mean throughput. Each arm ran twice on the same rack of 64 GB200 GPUs, in the order #9333, this PR, this PR, #9333. The trees were #9333 at `f56f7e6a9e` and this PR at `2698045acf`, which differ only in this change. The #9333 tree has the same dependency locks, hero model, training, and kernel code as `main` after #9333 merged. Each run restored the permanent hero `2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-30000` checkpoint with the production data mixture, batch 1024, sequence length 4096, and one process per GPU. Each run discarded 20 warmup updates and scored the 40 updates from 30020 through 30059. Every run sees the same batch at each step, so steps are compared across arms by step number.

| Configuration | Mean step time | Median step time | Mean iteration time | MFU | Runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| #9333 | 13.917 s | 13.906 s | 14.146 s | 28.21% | [a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-symab2-base-a-20260923), [b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-symab2-base-b-20260923) |
| This PR | 13.905 s | 13.882 s | 14.128 s | 28.23% | [a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-symab2-sym-a-20260923), [b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-symab2-sym-b-20260923) |

This PR was faster on 34 of 40 matched steps (sign test p = 8e-6). Two updates in run a took 14.96 s and 14.40 s. Excluding those steps, it saves 33 ms per update (standard error 6 ms), or 0.24%. Including them, mean training throughput improves by 0.09% (95% bootstrap interval −0.17% to +0.27%), and iteration throughput by 0.13%. None of the #9333 runs had an update slower than 14.18 s. In an earlier campaign on the same rack, updates slower than 14.3 s occurred in all three arms, including the #9366 control, so these runs do not show whether symmetric buffers cause them. Losses stayed finite. The largest matched-step loss difference was 0.00051, the same as between the two #9333 runs. An earlier three-run campaign, on the same rack and an earlier revision of #9333, measured a 0.32% mean gain ([a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-both-a-20260922), [b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-both-b-20260922), [c](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-both-c-20260922)).

Without the mask removal, symmetric buffers had no mean benefit: on PR #9228 revision `b688829e3d`, they measured −0.03% against the control ([a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-opt-fa4-symmetric-a-20260922), [b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-opt-fa4-symmetric-b-20260922), [c](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-opt-fa4-symmetric-c-20260922)), and slow updates in two repetitions erased an improvement in the median. A full [d768 run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-opt-d768-replayed-treatment-20260922) of 11,420 updates with both changes completed 20 dropless evaluations and matched the [historical control](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/validate9215-d768-20260917) to +0.000105 nats mean training loss.

Two risks remain untested at hero scale. The hero's parameters shard only within a rack, so each all-gather and reduce-scatter buffer should be the same size at 1 and 11 racks; whether XLA lowers any cross-rack gradient reduction as a symmetric-registered reduce-scatter or all-gather has not been checked. The dropless evaluator now also registers a symmetric window. #8861 showed that XLA resolves an address to the last window registered at the collective-memory arena base, so a smaller eval window can shadow the train step's; the d768 run passed its evaluations, but the hero shape has not been tested with interleaved evaluation.

Draft until those checks run.

topics.title: [data] Add a shared Common Crawl WARC layer
topics.body:
Add a shared Common Crawl discovery, planning, and fetch layer. Discovery scans URL Index Parquet partitions and writes a reusable manifest of selected records. Planning coalesces nearby records within each WARC, using a 1 MiB gap, and packs ranges into 256 MiB source-local fetch tasks. Sparse records remain singleton ranges and use the same fetch path.

Fetch validates the exact HTTP 206 response and Content-Range, resumes partial range downloads, bounds compressed records and decoded payloads, and fails if any planned record is missing. Parsed records are verified against the indexed URL and content digest. WARC record IDs are also checked when the index provides them; recent CC-MAIN and supplemental indexes may omit that field.

The shared layer supports multiple CC-MAIN and CC-SUPPLEMENTAL snapshots without coalescing or packing across sources. Candidate selection and document extraction remain pipeline-specific. The DOCX pipeline now uses the shared discovery manifest, planner, and coalesced fetch tasks.

Part of #7736 and should help with #7616.

🤖 Two blocking findings from a local review. Both are checked against live Common Crawl data, not just against the diff.

## 1. `discover_index_partition` cannot read a CC-MAIN index

`common_crawl_plan.py:318-322` adds `warc_record_id` to the required columns when `index_kind` is `MAIN`. The CC-MAIN columnar index does not have that column. I read the Arrow schema of `part-00000` under `subset=warc` for five crawls:

| crawl | columns | `warc_record_id` |
|---|---|---|
| CC-MAIN-2017-04 | 25 | absent |
| CC-MAIN-2020-05 | 29 | absent |
| CC-MAIN-2024-33 | 30 | absent |
| CC-MAIN-2025-05 | 30 | absent |
| CC-MAIN-2025-38 | 30 | absent |

Run against `cc-index/table/cc-main/warc/crawl=CC-MAIN-2025-05/subset=warc/part-00000-88b30a59-....parquet`:

```
ValueError: Index partition is missing required columns: ['warc_record_id']
```

The same partition with `index_kind=SUPPLEMENTAL` reads fine and yields records, so the record-ID requirement is the only thing blocking MAIN.

The PR body says record IDs are checked "when the index provides them", but the code makes the field mandatory for MAIN in two places: the column check above, and `main_record_from_index_row` -> `_canonical_record_id`, which raises on `None`.

If no index supplies `warc_record_id`, then `CommonCrawlIndexKind`, `MainIndexedRecord`/`SupplementalIndexedRecord`, the two expectation types, the two `*_from_index_row` factories, `verify_url_index_record`/`verify_supplemental_record`, `_canonical_record_id` and `_comparable_record_id` all exist to validate a field that never arrives. Collapsing to one record type and one verification function drops roughly 150 lines and makes the MAIN path work.

The transport path itself is correct. I built a two-record coalesced range from live CDX rows in CC-MAIN-2025-05 (906 B gap) and ran `CommonCrawlClient.fetch_range` against `data.commoncrawl.org`. It returned both records with digests matching the index.

## 2. Discovery drops selected rows silently

`common_crawl_plan.py:328-335` catches `ValueError` from record normalization and continues, with no log and no counter. Everything downstream is strict about lost records: `_parse_planned_records` raises `MissingPlannedRecordError` when a range omits one. This is the only place where selected records can disappear unnoticed.

A null `content_digest`, or a change in digest encoding, would make every row fail normalization. Discovery would write an empty `records.parquet`, the planner would emit zero tasks, and the run would report success. `AGENTS.md` says not to swallow exceptions.

Related: `discover_index_partition` is the only function in the PR that touches a real index, and it has no test. That is how (1) got past 50 passing tests.

> Nice!! Thank you. Could you pls restructure this as a Zephyr + StepSpec to follow existing patterns?

Thanks for the feedback! @ravwojdyla 

The discovery and planning stages have now been restructured as StepSpec in [#7919](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7919).

I was thinking the fetch step should remain as is to allow different pipelines define their own custom FetchStep while relying on this module to provide the reusable payload fetch functions.

Also updated the pr to make record_id optional and keep a count of records skipped during disscovery

topics.title: [levanter] Vectorize FA4 SM100 segment mask and zero accumulators in prep
topics.body:
This PR changes two parts of the SM100 FA4 kernels. The forward evaluates the document segment mask 32 columns at a time. The backward zeroes its fp32 accumulators the same way as upstream FA4 and no longer launches scalar zero-fill kernels. Before this change, the forward for document-masked local attention at hero shapes was about 1.7x slower than upstream FA4 varlen. Now the forward is within 5% of upstream.

The vectorized mask_mod builds keep-bitmasks with `r2p_bitmask_below` and `r2p_bitmask_above`. Its output is bitwise equal to the output of the scalar mask. In the backward, the preprocess kernel clears the dQ accumulator while it computes the row dot products. dK and dV start from an XLA zeros buffer that the kernel receives through `input_output_aliases`. Callers give the aliases to `cutlass_call` as a tuple of pairs, because the kernel cache key must be hashable. `cutlass_call` converts them to the dict that `cutlass.jax` expects. SM90 and SM120 keep the current zero-fill path.

Kernel measurements on one GB200 at hero shapes (median 16K rows):

| Metric | Before | After | Upstream varlen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local-layer forward | 3.16 ms | 1.96 ms | 1.87 ms |
| Local-layer fwd+bwd | 10.23 ms | 8.97 ms | |
| Projected attention cost | 0.777 s/step | 0.672 s/step | |

Output, dq, dk and dv match an fp32 reference with the same relative error as before. That error is 2.0e-3 to 2.6e-3, which is the bf16 rounding floor. The FA4 test file passes on GPU.

The end-to-end test ran on one GB200 NVL72 rack, restored from hero step 240000. At 16K context, the step time goes from 13.055 to 12.956 s/step (+0.76% tokens/s). The loss stays inside same-code noise, and the drop fraction does not change. A rank-0 trace shows that the attention kernels are 0.23 s/step faster. Peak memory increases by 0.5 GB because of the aliased dK/dV buffers.

The remaining gap to upstream is about 0.035 s/step, and it is in the backward. This backward uses 1-CTA with the scalar mask. The upstream backward uses 2-CTA.

topics.title: [datakit] Release the shared Zephyr pool after its last stage
topics.body:
Release the shared Zephyr pool when its last stage succeeds, so idle shared workers stop holding hosts needed by dedicated pools. `run_reference_steps` runs normalization before starting the shared pool; a watcher thread calls `ZephyrContext.shutdown()` after every step in `DatakitSteps.shared_pool_steps` succeeds. `ZephyrDatakitSteps` and `DecontaminationSteps` each list the stages that receive the shared context. If the watcher's status check raises, the run fails with that error. All three ferries use this path through `run_reference_ferry`, as does `reference_pipeline.py --target all`. The shared pool uses `_IdleWorkerPolicy.RETAIN`, so it previously kept every acquired worker until the DAG ended: up to 512 workers (2 CPU / 16 GiB each) on v5e hosts, while the embed, quality, fuzzy-cluster, and store pools waited for hosts.

Reduce the tier-1 store worker from 4 CPU / 32 GiB RAM / 64 GiB disk to 2 CPU / 8 GiB RAM / 16 GiB disk. A store task with one normalized shard peaks below 2 GiB RAM and spills below 1 GiB. On 2026-10-12, the old shape received 1 of 106 workers; the new shape received 12 workers in 1 minute.

On the fixed code, tier 1 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153556`) succeeded in 56 minutes. Tier 3 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153605`) succeeded, and its shared pool stopped at 19:30 UTC after fuzzy dedup. Tier 3 took 5h47m, exceeding the 20,700-second CI wait. On a busy cluster, the shared pool received only 275 of its 512 workers, and tokenization took 2h37m, compared with 37 minutes on 2026-10-05.

The tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers drop from 16 CPU / 128 GiB / 64 GiB disk to 8 CPU / 64 GiB / 32 GiB, with 64 instead of 32 workers, so the task count stays at 512. Only one of the larger workers fits on a v5e host. On 2026-10-13 the verify workers waited 3h46m for hosts, and the tier-3 ferry took 7h30m. At 16 tasks per worker, cluster text peaked at 66 GiB and verify at 26 GiB.

The three tiers passed in CI on this branch. Tier 1 took 56 minutes, and tier 2 took 1h51m. Tier 3 (`/runner/iris-run-job-20261013-165715`) took 2h25m, with 36 minutes for fuzzy verification. This is much less than the 20,700-second CI wait.

The tier concurrency groups now include `github.ref`, so a run started on a branch and the scheduled run on main do not cancel each other.

Fixes https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10047. Part of https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10059.

🤖 Changed the title to `[datakit] Release the shared Zephyr pool after its last stage` and removed the `---` footer from the body.

🤖 Holistic review of 781c86817111af521068d874daae8aace3f99fc0.

The PR starts the shared Zephyr pool after the normalize steps and stops it once every shared-pool stage succeeds. It also shrinks the tier-1 store and tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers and scopes the canary concurrency groups by ref. The design fits the existing `ZephyrContext` lifecycle: `shutdown()` is idempotent, and a later `execute()` raises `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`. `test_shared_pool_is_held_only_between_normalize_and_its_last_stage` passes locally and checks the ordering this PR depends on. Nothing blocks merging.

**Should fix**
1. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1147` `shared_pool_steps` is a second, hand-written list of the steps that `zephyr_datakit_steps` and `decontamination_steps` built with `zephyr_context`. The list is complete today. A future stage that gets `zephyr_context=zephyr_context` but is left off this list will run after the release and fail with `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`, hours into a tier-3 ferry. Fix: have each builder return its own list, for example a `shared_pool_steps` property on `ZephyrDatakitSteps` (exact_dedup, tokenize, minhash, fuzzy_dedup) and on `DecontaminationSteps` (bloom, drop_sets, marks), and set `shared_pool_steps=zephyr_steps.shared_pool_steps + decontamination.shared_pool_steps`. The membership then lives next to the code that passes in the context.
2. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1210` If `step_is_built` raises inside `_release_shared_pool`, for example on a transient object-store error reading a `StatusFile`, the daemon thread exits. `threading.excepthook` prints the traceback to stderr, `watcher.join()` returns normally, and the pool keeps its workers until the DAG ends. That is the #10047 behavior again, and no failure is reported. Fix: submit the watcher through a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` and call `future.result()` after `stop.set()`, so the exception reaches the caller. Alternatively, catch the error, log it, and retry on the next poll.

**Claims versus evidence**
3. PR body, "Fixes #10059": the first draft kept #10059 open for capacity, because one tier-3 run on a busy cluster took 5h47m and tokenization alone took 2h37m. The upgrade to "Fixes" rests on a single 2h25m CI run (`/runner/iris-run-job-20261013-165715`). The fuzzy-worker change fixes the 128 GiB placement failure that #10059 records. topics.title: [RL] Train Snowball curricula with separate Megatron reference nodes
topics.body:
Train Snowball curriculum policies on Megatron with separate reference nodes. The role plan derives seven-node smoke and ten-node full allocations from four policy nodes, two reference nodes and the rollout engines. `SNOWBALL_POLICY` selects recomputation, optimizer offload, checkpoint sharding and host memory; the MuonH presets select the pipeline layout and one-sequence microbatches.

Curriculum and async recipes share one parallelism type and select Megatron in their templates. Curriculum construction checks policy, reference and tuning geometry against the assigned GPUs. Launch preflight requires equal forward and training microbatch sizes. Async node counts come from the role plan.

Curriculum presets set `hf_save_interval` to `max_steps` so the final checkpoint carries the HF export request consumed by the launcher’s terminal conversion. The R4 and R5 Snowball MuonH presets use the pinned MarinSkyRL main revision `8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68`, which supports their MuonH gradient clipping at `1.0`.

The [H100 AdamW smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-curriculum-rl-snowball-naive-snowball-smoke-2026.10.17.10163-coordinator-f8096ba0%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-curriculum-rl-snowball-naive-snowball-smoke-2026.10.17.10163-0f4cc23f66d2) at the pinned runtime completes four nonzero optimizer updates, post-update engine syncs and a step-4 Megatron checkpoint. A [separate CPU job](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-snowball-pin8ab-checkpoint4-verify-20261017) confirms nonempty checkpoint shards, policy metadata and a step-4 HF export request pointing to that checkpoint.

A [Snowball MuonH smoke](https://wandb.ai/atqamar-oa/marin-curriculum-rl/runs/e2hv9s5y) at MarinSkyRL revision `42fbd4e` completes four nonzero updates, post-update engine syncs and a step-4 checkpoint with four pipeline stages and gradient clipping configured at `1.0`.

Launch-document checks load each rendered document through MarinSkyRL’s launcher and validate its trainer configuration. These run on an H100 worker, except the TaskSession checks, which use CPU dependencies.

### Model and workload scope

| Launcher and models | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Async Snowball | All three presets pass the launch-document checks; the public bootstrap tests check rollout-buffer translation. |
| Curriculum Qwen3-0.6B and Snowball | Qwen smoke/full and all six Snowball presets pass the launch-document checks. The public regression rejects Snowball on the incompatible default smoke scale and validates its separate-reference launch document. |
| Online EAGLE Snowball and its draft trainer | Both presets pass the launch-document checks with their draft-trainer allocation. |
| Iceball Qwen3 | The RL document passes the launch-document checks; pipeline construction tests check its artifact handoffs. |
| CatCount Qwen2.5 base/instruct and Qwen3 | Synchronous and asynchronous Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct launch documents pass the launch-document checks; existing launcher tests construct every listed model selection. |
| TaskSession validation | Whole-episode and step modes pass the launch-document checks; data and artifact-identity tests pass. |

topics.title: [vllm histograms] Store and query cumulative family snapshots
topics.body:
Store cumulative histograms as one record per engine and family. The opt-in Rigging publisher preserves collected integer bins, bounds, and collection metadata using existing `kind=histogram` records and nullable `body_json`. Raw histogram observations and the scalar publisher retain their behavior. No new record kind, table, column, backfill, or database/schema migration is required.

The detailed and compact dashboard readers share publication validation and interval-delta logic for scalar, structured, and mixed histories, including output length and time per output token. Equivalent numeric bounds share schema identity for interval baselines. Duplicate checks retain the original encoded bounds, so differing copies of one identified publication are excluded by both views. Dual writes are matched by publication identity. Counts support 0 through 2^63−1; unsupported source counts are reported as loss. Scalar counts at or above 2^53 are unavailable for exact deltas, and multiple bucket schemas withhold percentile/distribution estimates. The root DuckDB lock matches Grafana's 1.5.4.

The [design and local measurement report](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/773) documents the wire contract, ownership, and September 23–24, 2026 results: 6,208→832 data rows, 8→2 HTTP POSTs, 83.0% fewer compressed request bytes, and 180.17→33.50 seconds ingest in a four-engine, three-hour replay. Detailed client peak RSS was higher (441→474 MB). These historical measurements do not prove current-head performance, training speed, or #9382's seven-day/50-job ten-second target.

The companion producer is marin-community/MarinSkyRL#738. Activation requires the released Rigging API, frozen structured/dual delivery checks, regional-schema and external-consumer verification, server/reader deployment, and a bounded training canary. Part of #9382.

topics.title: [evals] Add an agent skill for registering evaluations
topics.body:
#6503 requires a defined path and agent skill for adding evaluations. `experiments/evaluation/README.md` documents the registry, but there is no task playbook that carries a new benchmark through configuration, behavior tests, a bounded live validation, durable records, and evaldash visibility.

Done when:

- `.agents/skills/add-eval/SKILL.md` describes how to register Evalchemy and Harbor evaluations on the shared launcher.
- The skill requires provenance, bounded dry-run and live validation, behavior-focused tests, and inspection of the terminal record and samples.
- The skill distinguishes served benchmarks from native training-time PPL/BPB evaluators and preserves the shared record/reporting boundary.
- Repository skill discovery lists the playbook and its referenced commands remain covered by tests or a maintained smoke path.

Part of #6503.

comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + actionability check (actionable: clear DoD)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR/issue)
- [x] Research eval registration surface + record/reporting boundary
- [x] Scope decision + proposed skill outline for review
- [ ] Human confirms outline / picks smoke-coverage path, then implement SKILL.md

**Scope:** authoring `add-eval/SKILL.md` is a new ~200-line canonical playbook (new artifact, >100 lines). Two of its DoD points need a maintainer decision before it becomes guidance, so this is an analysis-first comment, not an autonomous PR.

**Research**

Two separate eval systems the skill must keep distinct (the DoD "served vs native training-time PPL/BPB" point):

- **Served launcher** — `experiments/evaluation/`. One serve, N evals against the shared endpoint, one `record.json` per eval sharing a `group_id`, ingested by evaldash. This is what "registering an evaluation" means here.
- **Native training-time PPL/BPB** — `experiments/evals/task_configs.py` driven by Levanter's `eval_harness.py`, run inside training, not served, with its own reporting path. The skill should say "not this" and point here.

Registration surface for served evals is small: add an `EvalchemyDefinition`/`HarborDefinition` to `EVALS`, optionally add its key to a suite; add the model via a YAML catalog file or the Python factory. The record → evaldash boundary is one-directional: launchers write records, never touch Postgres.

**Relevant code**
- [`evaluation/evals.py#L33-L134`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L33) — `EvalchemyDefinition`/`HarborDefinition`, task flags (`generation`, `unsafe_code`, `completion_only`)
- [`evaluation/evals.py#L141`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L141) — `EVALS`, `SMOKE_EVALS`, `CORE_EVALS`, `SUITES`
- [`evaluation/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/README.md) — launcher, records/samples, Harbor, "Adding a model or eval"
- [`marin/evaluation/records.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py) + [`samples.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/samples.py) — `record.json` (provenance, `group_id`, `jobs`, `log_tails`), `EvalSample`
- [`infra/evaldash/src/results_db.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/evaldash/src/results_db.py) — `eval_runs`/`eval_metrics` ingest; the reporting side of the boundary
- [`experiments/evals/task_configs.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/task_configs.py) + [`levanter/eval_harness.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval_harness.py) — native training-time PPL/BPB (the "not served" path)

**Proposed skill outline**

`.agents/skills/add-eval/SKILL.md`, one section per DoD bullet:

1. **When to use / when not** — served benchmark on the shared launcher vs native training-time PPL/BPB. Route the latter to `experiments/evals/`.
2. **Register the eval** — Evalchemy: add an `EvalchemyDefinition` to `EVALS` (`EvalTaskConfig` task/shots/alias; flags `generation`, `unsafe_code`, `completion_only`); Harbor: add a `HarborDefinition` naming its `hf://` repo + revision, needs `DAYTONA_API_KEY`. Add the key to a suite in `SUITES` when it belongs to a group.
3. **Register the model if missing** — YAML under `serve/models/<org>/<model>.yaml` (bulk) or the factory in `models.py`; set `resource_hint`, `serve`, `generation`, `agent`, `tokenizer` for object-store exports.
4. **Provenance + bounded validation** — `--dry-run` (prints the resolved plan, submits nothing), then bounded live (`--limit`, capped smoke like `tb2-lite` for agentic), then confirm the terminal `record.json` (`status`, per-task metrics, `group_id`, `jobs`, `log_tails`) and inspect exported `EvalSample` parquet.
5. **Behavior test** — extend the endpoint-driven pattern in [`tests/evaluation/test_evaluation.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/tests/evaluation/test_evaluation.py) (`test_evaluate_batch_persists_failures_and_continues_on_the_same_endpoint`) — a real registry entry resolving/recording, not a tautology. No mocks.
6. **Record/reporting boundary** — the skill states launchers only write records; evaldash ingests. Do not add DB reads to a launcher.
7. **Discovery** — add the skill dir so it lists in skill discovery, following the frontmatter format of existing skills (e.g. `add-dataset/SKILL.md`).

**Two decisions I need before writing it**

1. **Coverage path.** DoD wants "referenced commands remain covered by tests or a maintained smoke path." Which is canonical: the existing `tests/evaluation/` behavior tests, a `--evals smoke --dry-run` plan-resolution check, or a live `tb2-lite`/smoke run gated to CI? Default I would take: the `tests/evaluation/` behavior test plus a `--dry-run` resolution check (no cluster), named in the skill.
2. **Provenance scope.** Confirm this means the `record.json` provenance/`group_id` fields, not a separate lineage requirement.

Confirm the outline and pick (1)/(2) and I will open the PR.

topics.title: Instruction Following post DPO
topics.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment tests whether DPO on IFBench-style preference data improves instruction following without overfitting to IFBench or damaging IFEval. The first completed Tulu-3 8B DPO runs built the shared IFBench/IFEval evaluation path, trained strict/loose/soft preference arms, and found a real positive signal: all DPO arms improved IFBench_test strict pass-all over the Tulu base, with the loose arm best on IFBench (+9.33 percentage points strict), while IFEval stayed flat-to-up. The issue is still open because the stronger paper-style full-train strict dataset and LR sweep were launched next, but no later result has been recorded in the issue. Current recommendation: treat IFBench-targeted DPO as promising on Tulu, but do not conclude the full recipe until the full-coverage LR sweep results are added.

### Helpful links
- Initial Tulu DPO result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5244#issuecomment-2846928782
- W&B project: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/ifbench_dpo
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

DPO against a narrow instruction-following spec may improve benchmark compliance while degrading broader instruction following. This project tracks whether IFBench-targeted DPO actually preserves or improves instruction-following behavior when evaluated on both IFEval and IFBench.

IFEval is the continuity baseline. IFBench is the primary target because it is the broader, more adversarial instruction-following benchmark for this work. We should compare base instruct models, external DPO models, and our DPO checkpoints under the same generation and scoring harness.

## Hypothesis or Goal

North star: improve IFBench and IFEval without creating a model that only overfits the IFBench verifier/spec.

Initial goals:

- Train DPO on preference pairs derived from IFBench-style pass/fail signals.
- Evaluate every candidate on both IFEval and IFBench with consistent chat templates, stop tokens, and generation config.
- Track whether DPO gains are isolated to IFBench or transfer to IFEval.
- Test whether mixing SFT data with DPO data regularizes the model toward general instruction following while retaining IFBench gains.

### Links

- Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/dpo_sft_codex.md`
- Shared project notes: `.agents/projects/dpo_sft.md`
- W&B project: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/ifbench_dpo

## Results

Pending. Current runs include Tulu-3 8B DPO baselines and learning-rate sweeps on the paper-strict IFBench preference dataset.

topics.title: [finestore] Prefetch small compaction inputs concurrently
topics.body:
FineStore compactions with at most 16 MiB of compressed input now fetch whole shards with up to 16 concurrent reads and reuse those bytes for schema and row reads. Larger compactions keep their bounded streaming reads.

[A live evaluation](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Feval-20261017-015918-qwen3-8b-59475eeeb8a94886a01e373e84d3f073-3066d84b%2Feval-drop-5c76ab07) took 9.83 seconds to compact 17 shards containing 128 rows and 196 KB. Its isolated Evalchemy environment was already running `marin-finestore 0.2.197.dev38989978700`, including #10209 and #10216. Compaction still reopened shards for schema, footer, and data reads, issuing those reads serially.

In a synthetic benchmark with 17 small shards and 100 ms per simulated S3 request, total compaction time falls from 5.76 to 0.85 seconds and GETs fall from 54 to 20. A read-only comparison in the evaluation container over six active shards (75 KB, 45 rows) reduced schema and row loading from 3.02 to 0.10 seconds; that measurement excludes output writes and manifest publication.

topics.title: [grug] Fix AMD Pallas flash attention on packed and one-device meshes
topics.body:
`gpu_pallas_triton_flash` failed at trace time on packed batches under an explicit mesh. `_key_lower_bounds` concatenated a replicated `jnp.ones((batch, 1))` with the batch-sharded segment-ID comparison, and explicit sharding rejects operands with different shardings (`ShardingTypeError: All operands should have the same sharding`). Grug's data loader shards segment IDs by batch, so every packed run with this backend failed, on one GPU or many. The first column is now built from the segment IDs, so it shares their sharding.

It also failed on one-device meshes. The wrapper skipped `shard_map` when no axis of size greater than 1 partitioned q, and `pallas_call` rejects operands whose type names a mesh axis (`ValueError: sharded ref ... can only be sliced along unsharded axes`). Grug's meshes keep length-1 axes in every spec, so every single-device Grug or Snowball run with this backend failed. The wrapper now skips `shard_map` only when q's spec names no mesh axis, so Auto meshes keep their current path.

Two regression tests cover the fixes, and each failed on main with the error above: a packed, batch- and head-sharded run on a 4-device CPU mesh, and a packed run on a one-device Grug mesh.

Supersedes #10126, which fixed only the one-device case.

Part of #9812

topics.title: Add a tiled copy-paste loss for July MoE experiments
topics.body:
Add a target-only copy-paste loss for July MoE experiments. To predict token t+1, the head attends only to observed tokens at positions ≤t in the same packed document and sums repeated-token probability. The copy gate competes with the vocabulary logits; a learned sink returns part of the copy probability to the native vocabulary distribution. Rematerialized query tiles bound score storage while retaining quadratic arithmetic.

The loss accepts native vocabulary NLL and log partition with gradients, leaving vocabulary-kernel choice and loss masking to the caller. Independent dense-mixture tests cover values, gradients and causal/document isolation. The historical July training adapter and d512/d768 run evidence are linked from the issue. This initial draft does not integrate with the current trainer or provide optimized vocabulary kernels or generation/cache support. Current Marin's vocabulary backend selection differs from the pinned research runtime and needs separate integration checks.

Part of #10229.

Research provenance: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151 and originating task https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99 (`ordered_paragraph_template@1`).

One bounded retry, `/romain/snowball-tpu-causal-4e9a9782-01a13250-r1`, was submitted at 01:11:54 UTC after the live pool cleared backoff. It also never allocated. It was still pending at 01:43:02 UTC and was cancelled, then verified killed. The 30-minute queue deadline was checked about one minute late; no worker had started. Neither causal job produced correctness or score results. These are candidate results. All six checks still need to pass at the final Marin revision after the backend fixes merge.

The original successful serving report was recovered from the exact submitted callable: `gs://marin-us-east5/tmp/ttl=30d/snowball-parity/reports/e64e0adbb7024c5d86b13a4bc5661c8b/vllm-tpu.json` (SHA-256 `186c6393d2e49cbef6bf5a45165b5a3b44dada512c6374e922e73fd04c312a17`). A small regional CPU job, `/romain/snowball-tpu-serving-preview-4e9a9782-01a13250`, rechecked all 64 saved observations inside us-east5. Against the current native candidate scores, the bucket maxima are 0.032312, 0.054535, 0.114590, 0.593274 and 0.420621. `specialized-mmmlu-05` fails the unchanged 4K limit (0.114590 > 0.10); all other cases satisfy the existing rules. This reanalysis does not justify a reference update or count as a new serving run. If the causal comparison justifies the current native scores, this case needs a scoped serving fix and a full rerun. topics.title: [sft] Add the GLM 5.3 Harbor trace generation driver
topics.body:
Generate k=8 GLM 5.3 trajectories for TMax and SWE-smith pool tasks with
Harbor, plus v0/GLM relay episodes in which the v0 student acts until a trigger
(a completion claim, a format error or the context budget) hands the turn to
GLM. Each family runs under its eval-campaign Harbor policy, whose YAMLs and
Harbor/Evalchemy pins come from #9569; the runs used that branch, and this
driver needs it merged first. Inside the run, a local OpenAI-compatible proxy
routes each request to the student or the GLM bulk relay and logs every request
and reply per trial. rebuild_traces turns those logs into one row per
conversation with turn authors, triggers and per-author token counts.

The proxy re-resolves a backend endpoint that refuses connections. A preempted
v0 server moves hosts, and the address remote_inference resolved at start goes
stale (#10237). A run fails when more than 20% of its trials raised without
any proxy reply, since that means a backend was down, not that the agent failed.

Capability URLs are bearer credentials, so every output is scrubbed of Iris
capability tokens before it is written, including JWTs split across escaped
line breaks. scrub_run re-checks finished runs, and publish_hf refuses to
upload a row that still holds one. During the agent phase the sandbox reaches
only the proxy, and mini-swe-agent installs from pinned constraints. The
null, network and tool-env probe agents record what a sandbox can reach.

The traces from these runs are published as
open-athena/GLM-5.3-tmax-swesmith-k8-traces-2026.10.

topics.title: Marin Eval Policy (2026-10-16)
topics.body:
## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Sept 24, 2026: 18 non-agentic benchmarks, 8 Harbor agentic benchmarks, and 4 reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks.

## Complete eval list, with hyperparameters
